title.narrative: Crisis Medical Response for Lebanon - AUB

description.narrative: (Lebanon): Through the Crisis Medical Response (CMR Lebanon) activity, which was awarded in January 2024 using Complex Crises Funds, USAID has supported the American University of Beirut Medical Center (AUBMC), to pre-position medical supplies and equipment and prepare their workforce to respond successfully to mass casualty incidents. To leverage and complement these prior investments and given the dire economic context facing Lebanon and recent fighting between Hizballah and Israel that has led to even more significant economic losses, university hospitals are now struggling to cope with high costs and high volatility of availability of diesel fuel for generators due to lack of reliable grid-provided electricity. As such, FY24 assistance will support the AUBMC in purchasing American-made solar panels to promote energy independence and long-term sustainable solutions, cut costs, and save critical resources. This $5M meets the $5M directive in the 653a report for hospital energy programs.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Population Survey in Nepal

description.narrative: The overall goal of the Population Based Survey (PBS) is to provide USAID/Nepal, its U.S. Government inter-agency partners. the USAID Bureau for Food Security, USAID Missions, the Government of Nepal, and development partners with information on the current status of the Feed the Future population-based ZOI level indicators in Nepal. The survey is designed to (1) determine whether there has been statistically significant change over time in the Feed the Future phase one ZOI key outcome and impact indicatros, and (2) establish the baseline status of Feed the Future phase two ZOI indicators. Therefore, the 2018 Nepal ZOI survey is intended to serve both as an endline for Feed the Future phase one and a baseline for Feed the Future phase two in Nepal.

description.narrative: (Sri Lanka): .SCORE promotes reconciliation and social cohesion addressing underlying grievances that led to Sri Lanka's civil war, mistrust between ethnic and religious groups, and segregation in the political, economic, and cultural arena..SCORE addresses structural drivers that enable violent extremism. It acts as a change agent to Sinhalese Buddhist and Muslim communities in the Southern, Central, and Eastern Provinces, promote open dialogue, and extend support to coexistence societies and inter-religious committees to strengthen social harmony and religious tolerance. SCORE will partner with Ministry of Justice, transitional justice mechanisms such as Office of National Unity and Reconciliation, Office of Missing Persons (OMP)and Parliamentary select committees to address issues of communal and religious harmony, and national unity. It will support social media campaigns to counter fake news, social engineering, and radicalization of youth along religious lines, and provide sub-grants to religious networks to carry out social cohesion and reconciliation activities. Through small grants and technical assistance it will promote youth networks to strengthen the moderate youth voices in society through non-violent communication and inter-communal activities..To meet Sec. 7044(e)(1) requirements, it will explore an OMP partnership to provide capacity building, advisory support, document management, and technical assistance to help process a backlog of documentation. As an alternative, SCORE may train civil society and provide technical assistance to bolster capacity to create public awareness of the OMP, advocate for identification, and support family members of missing persons. . SCORE advances ICS Objective 2. $1.22 million within this IM contributes to the DRG Directive...

description.narrative: (Maldives): Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, Maldives, driven by a strong tourism sector, made significant strides in its economic development. Due to the economic impacts of COVID-19 and poorly planned and managed capital investments, Maldives now faces growing fiscal and debt risks.Through the Public Finance Management (PFM) activity, USAID supports improved budget management, public investment management, and domestic resource mobilization. This activity supports the Ministry of Finance to better manage public expenditure (with a performance-based budgeting system); improve public investment decisions; conduct high-quality macro-fiscal analysis, and conduct the incidence of taxes (i.e. a study on the effects of tax policies on prices and the distribution of utilities/welfare). The PFM activity also supports the government to streamline processes and adopt international best practices to reduce corruption. FY 2022 funding will allow PFM Maldives to continue these activities, reducing the risk of a debt crisis and of the country's vulnerability to coercive economic behavior by the People's Republic of China (PRC).Through the PFM activity, USAID advances the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 2.1: Strengthened public sector capacity to implement and sustain reforms that align with international norms, improve transparency, mitigate corruption, and increase opportunities for responsible international investment..

description.narrative: (Maldives): Following 30 years of authoritarian rule, Maldives held its first multi-party elections in 2008. Reforming and building institutions and consolidating democratic norms have been challenges in Maldives. In addition, Maldives is attempting to transition from a highly centralized government to one in which local island councils have a more meaningful role in the political sphere.Through the Strong and Inclusive Maldivian Democracy activity, USAID will use FY 2022 funds to strengthen the capacity of key national and local democratic institutions by providing assistance to the government to implement decentralization and justice sector reforms. In addition, USAID will build the capacity of civil society and media to engage in effective advocacy and oversight. To build a sustainable foundation for a strong and inclusive democracy, this activity will also support civic education and better connect Maldivian citizens with their government.Through this activity, USAID will work closely with government counterparts, including the President's Office and the Local Government Authority, to build the capacity of local councils and women's development committees to engage in participatory and inclusive development processes. USAID will partner with key institutions in the justice sector, including the Judicial Services Commission, the Maldives Judicial Academy, and the Maldives Bar Council, to increase the quality of justice administration and professionalism of legal practitioners. In turn, justice sector support will increase access to justice for marginalized communities.The activity advances Integrated Country Strategy Mission Goal 3: Supported the development of a resilient, diverse, and inclusive Maldivian democracy..

title.narrative: TB Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence - Trace TB

description.narrative: (India): ..The Ayushman Bharat Digital Health Mission (ABDM) aims to develop the backbone necessary to support the integrated digital health infrastructure of the country. This mechanism supports the building block of ABDM and builds the country's Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities to enhance the National TB Elimination Program to meet its goals...Using FY 2022 funds, Trace-TB will introduce AI solutions for TB that help strengthen the delivery of healthcare services, accelerate efforts to eliminate TB, and better respond to infectious diseases in India. This will be achieved through the following approaches: 1) create an enabling environment to adopt sustainable digital and AI solutions that address existing and emerging infectious diseases; 2) support research and development for innovative digital and AI solutions across the cascade of care to effectively manage infectious disease threats; and 3) demonstrate early adoption of efficient digital and AI solutions for existing and emerging infectious diseases..These interventions support the U.S. Government's Global Tuberculosis Strategy, which aims to reach every person with TB, cure those in need of treatment, and prevent the spread of disease and new infections. .

description.narrative: (India): ..Using FY 2022 funds, USAID/India will continue to support the India Partnership for Early Learning activity focusing on Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN). The activity will support the state governments and institutions by increasing their capacity to leverage and coordinate financial, human, and material resources to implement evidence-based service delivery in FLN. The ultimate objective is to steadily increase the percentage of students attaining age and grade appropriate proficiencies in the reading, math, cognitive, and social and emotional domains...The activity will build state/national government capability in designing and developing reporting systems, curriculum, classroom pedagogy, teacher training for "reading" instruction, and the use of education technology where appropriate. By identifying, institutionalizing, and scaling best practices, as well as investing in systemic processes such as teacher training and curriculum development the activity will not only be able to increase reading levels of an increased number of learners it will also reduce barriers to literacy and improve access to girls and women. These efforts together will ensure more learners who read at grade level. ..USAID/India will leverage innovative partnerships and financing strategies by engaging with the private sector and focusing on the development of innovative financing models to leverage private investment, Corporate Social Responsibility funds, grant capital, and philanthropic funds. The aim will be to accelerate enterprise-driven solutions to assist states in martialing successful managerial, operational, and technical strategies across the education value chain involving both public and private actors so that they can deliver high-quality foundational skills instruction to all students under their care, regardless of the type of primary or pre-primary school they attend..

description.narrative: (USAID South Asia Regional): .This is a partnership between USAID and a consortium with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and three national laboratories: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, National Renewable Energy Laboratory, and Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. It will support the Indo-Pacific Strategy and the U.S-India Climate and Clean Energy Agenda 2030 Partnership by undertaking analysis and modeling on energy sector opportunities throughout South Asia, equipping USAID and partner governments with information on clean energy transition opportunities and providing support for sustainable and secure energy markets across the Indo-Pacific. It will be a key mechanism to deliver on the Indo-Pacific Strategy as well on the Sustainable Growth Pillar under the Strategic Clean Energy Partnership, one of the two tracks under the U.S.-India Climate and Clean Energy Agenda 2030 Partnership. It facilitates access to technical expertise within DOE labs and other relevant USG and private sector partners for knowledge sharing to support Pillar 1 (Climate Actions) and Pillar 3 (Adaptation and Resilience) under the Climate Action and Finance Mobilization Dialogue.. .This mechanism will undertake to model the impact of changing economic and environmental conditions on the reliability of South Asia's power sector and assess aspects related to grid management. The consortium undertakes analyses to support the promotion of clean energy technologies, strengthen grid security and reliability for the clean energy transition, and assess the impacts of climate change on hydro-resources. It partners with institutions to strengthen their modeling and analytical capacity for clean energy. It will also leverage the U.S. partnership with India through collaborations with Indian technical institutions, including the India Energy Modeling Forum established with NITI Aayog (India's premier think tank), and explore higher education partnerships to promote clean energy and climate a

title.narrative: USAID Host and Impacted Community Resilience Activity - Development Innovation Ventures (DIV)

description.narrative: Development Innovation Ventures (DIV) provides grant funding to innovators and researchers to test new ideas, take strategic risks, build evidence of what works, and advance the best solutions. DIVs evidence-based, tiered-funding model embraces risk at early stages and mitigates risk at later stages, ensuring that funding is targeted to the most cost-effective innovations that can improve peoples lives. DIV takes a broad approach to innovation; innovations can be business models, products, behavioral interventions, applied research, or replications of proven innovations in novel environments.

description.narrative: (Mongolia): USAID's Mongolia Energy Governance (MEG) activity will advance shared U.S. and Mongolian priorities to mitigate the impacts of climate change and expand renewable energy use. With the energy sector at the core of Mongolia's national security and economic prosperity, USAID efforts will foster a modern, competitive, and sustainable energy sector that is less dependent on Russia and China to meet domestic energy needs. To facilitate a low carbon transition, USAID will: improve the operational and financial performance of electric utilities; accelerate policy and regulatory market reforms, expand public engagement, and employ best-value procurement methods; and encourage the adoption of modern technologies by boosting private sector investments on renewable and cleaner fuels, smart grids, and energy-efficient systems. USAID will advance the green energy revolution by engaging with the government, research institutions, private businesses, and the technology sector to encourage the adoption of renewable and low carbon energy sources and maximize the utilization of Mongolia's vast wind and solar energy base. To improve operations of electric utilities, USAID will enhance network upgrade and generation capability and the capacity to integrate new energy resources. USAID will assess cybersecurity vulnerabilities of electric utilities and develop a responsive investment strategy to reduce risks to the electricity grid and regional networks. To promote power market competitiveness, USAID will carry out public information and awareness campaigns and facilitate market-based retail electricity pricing. To ensure a gender-responsive transition to low carbon development, USAID will develop a strategic gender action plan, promote equal participation of women and men in utility operations, and support local pollution reduction policies.. .

description.narrative: (Cambodia): The Integrated Early Childhood Development (IECD) activity supports children to thrive and reach full developmental potential by promoting nurturing care for the most vulnerable newborns and young children, beginning with expectant mothers or expectant parents. IECD strengthens the capacity of community volunteers through training and mobilization to support households on nurturing care, child malnutrition and disability screening for children under five years of age. IECD also supports homestead food production by promoting home gardening for greater household consumption of nutritious foods, and income generation. The activity promotes best practices in water, hygiene and sanitation including the use of latrines and safe drinking water. IECD adapts existing resources and tools to improve and broaden developmental monitoring and early identification of children with developmental delays and disabilities, and to increase referral to quality, and sustainable services..As 22 percent of children under five years of age are stunted, this intervention is most appropriate through its multi-sectoral approach that strengthens nutrition service delivery at health facilities and in communities. USAID awarded IECD through a competitive process in which the offeror with the best value to the U.S. government was selected, in accordance with federal procurement regulations..This activity addresses the administration's "Advancing global health security and mitigating development and humanitarian impacts" priority by providing inclusive opportunities for livelihoods and addressing hunger and malnutrition. It also contributes to achieving the USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 Development Objective (DO) 2, "Health, education, and welfare of Cambodians improved through enhanced services" and DO1 "Inclusive and sustainable economic growth broadened."...

description.narrative: (China): This activity is in design. Specific interventions will be identified and the IM updated as more is determined...Activities may build urban resilience in China's secondary cities; provide technical support, tools and protocols for greenhouse gas accounting; support pollution reduction efforts in China's urban areas; promote the adoption of international best practices and standards in environmental policies and regulations to mitigate the environmental and social impacts of Chinese infrastructure investments domestically and internationally; and promote the acquisition of U.S. best practices, professional services and technologies to help solve China's extraordinary environmental challenges. Programming aims to enhance green business and economic opportunities for U.S. firms in the large and expanding Chinese market while continuing U.S. government's strategic partnership with China on environmental issues.

Objectives for China: USAID Mekong Safeguards aims to: (i) minimize negative environmental impacts of infrastructure projects by fostering more robust and consistent application of environmental, social, and governance standards; and (ii) encourage decision-makers to avoid unnecessary, harmful infrastructure through smart technologies, system-scale infrastructure planning, and innovations.

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): The Advanced Energy Partnership for Asia ("The Partnership") supports USAID's Asia Enhancing Development and Growth through Energy (Asia EDGE) initiative through the provision of U.S. technical leadership, expertise, and experience in advanced energy sector technologies and practices. The Partnership is an interagency agreement between USAID/RDMA and the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE's) national laboratories, led by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). .USAID/RDMA will use FY 2021 funds to continue supporting activities under the Partnership focusing on the development and deployment of tools, state-of-the-art approaches, and technical assistance to scale up advanced energy systems. The Partnership concentrates on key opportunities within partner countries, such as:.Utility performance: Improving energy utility planning and operational practices to increase efficiency and deploy advanced energy systems..A level playing field: Assisting governments in fostering supportive policy, legal and regulatory environments for private sector deployment and investment in clean energy systems..Data-driven decision-making: Increasing the availability and use of high-quality data to drive energy sector analysis and decision-making..Regional integration: Advancing regional energy system planning and operation practices to promote efficient and flexible cross-border energy trade..

description.narrative: (China): .The Mekong Sustainable Manufacturing Alliance activity will improve the competitiveness of the manufacturing sectors in the Mekong region through private sector partnerships and the application of robust environmental, social, and governance (ESG) safeguards and standards for manufacturers with operations in Mekong countries. FY 2021 funds will be used to promote private sector best practices that advance sustainable supply chains in order to minimize negative environmental impact on the local communities in the Mekong region, which, in many instances, is a result of PRC investments. The activity will work with brands in selected manufacturing sectors to increase their suppliers' capacity to adopt standards and improve their ESG performance. It will also work to catalyze regional opportunities for improving ESG performance by creating a regional private sector network and engaging with industry associations to increase competitiveness in the manufacturing sector. Anticipated results include strengthened sustainability and competitiveness, increased regional knowledge of manufacturing sector ESG best practices and resources, and a more level playing field for U.S. companies, while creating more secure supply chains. This activity will promote sustainable economic growth in the Mekong region with a focus on the manufacturing sector. It will provide an opportunity for companies in Lower Mekong countries to enter the global supply chain if they are able to meet international standards. This will foster sustainable and secure supply chains and improved natural resource management. .

title.narrative: Enhancing Equality in Energy for Southeast Asia

description.narrative: The activity aims to improve gender equality and inclusion in the energy sector by providing support to the energy sector across the focus countries. The EEE for SEA Activity will be implemented across 5 countries in the SEA region: Cambodia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, with implementation potential in 2 additional countries (Burma and Lao PDR). The overall goal of the Activity is to improve gender equality in the energy sector and achieve a sustainable and secure industry that contributes to womens empowerment. To achieve this goal, the EEE for SEA Activity is focusing on the following objectives: 1. Increase diversity of the energy sector workforce. 2. Support inclusive workplace environments. 3. Increase promotion and leadership opportunities for women.

description.narrative: (China): .The Mekong for the Future activity addresses the PRC government's policies and initiatives that negatively affect the sustainable management of natural resources in the Mekong region. The activity aims to increase transparency and access to data and information, and promote participation of civil society organizations in natural resources management. By increasing civil society participation in these processes, environmental governance in the region can become more inclusive, accountable, and transparent. FY 2021 funds will be used to engage with stakeholders, such as non-government organizations (NGOs), civil society organizations (CSOs), and media to strengthen their organizational capacity for policy analysis and advocacy, and promote CSO engagement in the decision-making processes. This greater transparency and inclusiveness will broaden the range of stakeholders holding their governments accountable and advocating for better policies to manage natural resources in a more sustainable manner at the national and regional levels... .

description.narrative: Asia Enhancing Development and Growth through Energy (Asia EDGE) is a U.S. Government-wide initiative to grow sustainable and secure energy markets throughout the Indo-Pacific region, which spans the California coast to the western shores of India, by helping governments expand energy access, promote energy diversification and trade, and strengthen energy security.

A Ásia Melhorando o Desenvolvimento e o Crescimento através da Energia (Asia EDGE) é uma iniciativa de todo o governo dos EUA para desenvolver mercados energéticos sustentáveis ​​e seguros em toda a região do Indo-Pacífico, que se estende da costa da Califórnia até a costa ocidental da Índia, ajudando os governos a expandir o acesso à energia, promover a diversificação e o comércio energético e fortalecer a segurança energética.

description.narrative: (Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)): .The ASEAN USAID Partnership Program is a demand-driven and.flexible program to advance shared priorities of the United States and ASEAN.through our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which is aligned closely with.the ASEAN Outlook for the Indo-Pacific. The Partnership Program is a key.platform for expanded engagement with ASEAN. Key objectives include supporting.inclusive economic growth, addressing transnational security challenges,.promoting good governance and strengthening capacity of ASEAN institutions. The.Partnership Program will continue working with ASEAN on key issues and emerging.technologies including the ASEAN Artificial Intelligence (AI) Roadmap and.Safety Network, strengthening cybersecurity capacity in the face of increasing.People's Republic of China (PRC) threats, raising standards in the critical.minerals sector and improving efficiency and volumes of intra-ASEAN and global.trade through the ASEAN Single Window (ASW). These priorities align with 2025.ASEAN Chair Malaysia's Priority Economic Deliverables. The Partnership Program.will strengthen ASEAN capacity to address key transnational security issues.including Trafficking in Persons (TIP), Preventing and Countering Violent.Extremism (PCVE), building ASEAN's capacity to respond to natural disasters,.strengthening the region's health security architecture and continue supporting.disability rights, women's empowerment and human rights. FY24 funding will.strengthen the capacity of the ASEAN Secretariat and the ASEAN entities to.better address the region's development challenges, enabling some organizations.to become direct recipients of USAID funding. These ASEAN-affiliated entities.work on diverse issues such as humanitarian assistance, climate change, public.health emergencies, human rights and disabilities. Assistance to ASEAN will.support all member states including high-income countries of Brunei Darussalam.and Singapore..

description.narrative: (Philippines): .USAID, through the YouthWorksPH activity, supports workforce development for youth ages 15-29 who are not in education, employment, or training by mobilizing local private sector resources to provide innovative and work-based training opportunities, and leveraging $4 from local partners for every $1 USAID invests in the program. ..Using higher education-earmarked resources, USAID will expand support to trainees and partner institutions to provide quality and relevant training to increase youth employment, in spite of the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and the challenges of virtual learning. USAID targets at least 1,500 youth to be recruited, trained, and deployed for on-the-job training, and/or placed in work opportunities, especially in growing industries. In addition, USAID aims to support at least one recognized industry body, sector skills council, localized government/industry/academic council, or industry association. USAID will also support the Workforce Development Summit to increase cooperation among key stakeholders in this sector. .Finally, USAID will help establish the learner management information system by providing technical assistance to the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, the Department of Trade and Industry, and the Department of Labor and Employment. USAID will assist in creating an application programming interface for a synchronized database on private sector-led training...

description.narrative: (Philippines): .In 2017, violent conflict erupted between ISIS-inspired militant groups and the Philippine military in Marawi, Muslim Mindanao, which displaced the city's entire population, creating economic and social shocks even in the environs. According to the UNCHR report, over 17,000 families remain displaced in Lanao, as a result of the Marawi conflict as of June 2021. The large population displacement stressed the limited capacity of local governments, created social divisions and disrupted the local economy that is largely agriculture-based. The underground economy in the area is evident, with reports of drugs, guns and human smuggling. Displaced communities are threatened by violent extremism, as resentment is exploited as part of the recruitment narrative. .The Marawi Response Project will utilize earmarked FY 2021 DRG funds to continue strengthening the social bonds of displaced citizens and their host communities, through non-cash micro-grants program. Partners will bring together displaced and host citizens in target barangays, organize them into community solidarity groups and help them to identify community problems that can be addressed by the grant support for town halls, civic engagement training sessions and forums with local government. Funds will also be used to bolster the political participation of displaced communities to include voter education and election monitoring in the run up to the 2022 national and local polls. . .. .. .

(Filipinas): En 2017, estalló un conflicto violento entre grupos militantes inspirados por ISIS y el ejército filipino en Marawi, Mindanao musulmán, que desplazó a toda la población de la ciudad, creando conmociones económicas y sociales incluso en los alrededores. Según el informe de ACNUR, más de 17.000 familias siguen desplazadas en Lanao como resultado del conflicto de Marawi en junio de 2021. El gran desplazamiento de población puso de relieve la capacidad limitada de los gobiernos locales, creó divisiones sociales y perturbó la economía local que se basa en gran medida en la agricultura. La economía sumergida en la zona es evidente, con denuncias de drogas, armas y tráfico de personas. Las comunidades desplazadas se ven amenazadas por el extremismo violento, ya que el resentimiento se explota como parte de la narrativa del reclutamiento. El Proyecto de Respuesta de Marawi utilizará fondos DRG asignados para el año fiscal 2021 para continuar fortaleciendo los vínculos sociales de los ciudadanos desplazados y sus comunidades de acogida, a través de un programa de microsubvenciones no monetarias. Los socios reunirán a los ciudadanos desplazados y de acogida en los barangays seleccionados, los organizarán en grupos de solidaridad comunitaria y los ayudarán a identificar los problemas comunitarios que pueden abordarse mediante subvenciones para ayuntamientos, sesiones de capacitación sobre participación cívica y foros con el gobierno local. Los fondos también se utilizarán para reforzar la participación política de las comunidades desplazadas para incluir la educación de los votantes y el seguimiento electoral en el período previo a las elecciones nacionales y locales de 2022. . .. .. .

description.narrative: (Pacific Islands Regional): .This USAID activity strengthens local civil society organizations (CSOs) to address second order impacts of COVID-19, which include loss of livelihoods and severe financial strains for governments and communities. These challenges have exacerbated existing development challenges related to climate and disaster vulnerability, natural resource management, and limited access to safe drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. Sub-grants to CSOs will support communities' unique challenges, as well as recovery from COVID-19 second order impacts. Sub-grants will be multi-sectoral and offer communities increased resilience to disasters and climate risks, enhanced livelihoods, improved access to WASH services, and more sustainable natural resources management and biodiversity conservation. To increase WASH access, sub-grants may support basic WASH training in rural communities; planning, design, and mobilization of funds for critical WASH facilities; and approaches to increase the resilience of water infrastructure for better disaster preparedness and response. To strengthen biodiversity conservation and help address the economic impacts of COVID-19, sub-grants will target natural resource dependent communities and support various interventions such as promoting alternative sustainable livelihoods in coastal marine, coral reef, and forest areas...This USAID activity contributes to the U.S. vision for an open, interconnected, resilient, and secure Indo-Pacific by espousing transparency and accountability in managing sub-grants, thereby promoting good governance across the region. USAID will empower local leaders and communities and enable enterprise-driven growth. By improving local organizations' managerial, financial, and organizational capacity, as well as facilitating peer-to-peer learning and network building opportunities, USAID will advance sustainable development throughout the region...

title.narrative: Strengthening Competitiveness, Agriculture, Livelihoods, and Environment (SCALE) - Natural Resources Management (NRM)

description.narrative: (Pacific Islands Regional): .This USAID activity contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions or improving the conditions to enable such reductions by providing technical assistance and support to help the Solomon Islands improve natural resource management (NRM), particularly forest governance. USAID's SCALE-NRM activity addresses unsustainable forestry practices in the Solomon Islands by strengthening the capacity of community-based organizations to mobilize people and local government structures around sustainable and inclusive NRM initiatives; develop opportunities for alternative livelihoods from agroforestry and conservation; and strengthen local capacity to effectively plan, manage, and protect forests...With FY 2022 funds, USAID will support tribal and community-driven forest restoration projects, assist communities with alternative livelihoods to logging, progress in establishing two payment for ecosystem services schemes, conduct analyses and develop tools to aid decision-making on climate change, continue to work for the passage of two ordinances-the Forest Business License Ordinance and the Environment and Conservation Ordinance-to support conservation efforts, and strengthen provincial- and ward-level institutions in implementing climate mitigation and forest conservation actions. .This activity will contribute to the Indo-Pacific Strategy by strengthening natural resource governance in the Solomon Islands. . .... ...

title.narrative: Pacific Regional Initiative and Support for More Effective Counter-Trafficking in Persons (Pacific RISE CTIP)

description.narrative: (Pacific Islands Regional): .The Pacific Island region is reported as a source, transit point, and destination for human trafficking for purposes of sexual exploitation and forced labor particularly in local extractive industries such as fishing, logging, and mining. The annual U.S. State Department Trafficking in Persons report examines government actions to counter trafficking in persons relative to the minimum standards set in the Trafficking Victim Protection Act. The 2022 report's major finding is that a number of governments of Pacific Island Countries (PICs) do not fully meet the minimum standards for the elimination of trafficking. Papua New Guinea, Palau, and Tonga are on the Tier 2 watch list; and Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, Republic of Marshall Islands and Vanuatu are classified as Tier 2...This activity aims to combat trafficking in persons in the PICs through interventions that will reduce vulnerability to trafficking, enhance local and community-based mechanisms and strategies to prevent trafficking, provide adequate protection services and sustainable solutions to victims and survivors, and strengthen the capacity of relevant actors to expand access to legal services and remedies for victims and survivors, and prosecute traffickers. This activity will apply a holistic and multi-sectoral approach taking into consideration the priorities across the four pillars of the USG counter-trafficking strategy (prevention, protection, prosecution, and partnerships), the USAID Trafficking in Persons Policy, and the recommendations for the PICs as stated in the U.S. Department of State Annual Trafficking in Persons Reports..

title.narrative: Papua New Guinea Sustainable Landscapes Activity

description.narrative: (Papua New Guinea): USAID, through the Papua New Guinea Sustainable Landscapes (PNGSL) activity, will bolster PNG's ongoing efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, enhance carbon sequestration, and address COVID-19 impacts through technical assistance and training that will increase capture of its forests' value and align economic development policies and incentives with natural resource conservation to benefit local communities. Interventions will seek the following objectives:.Strengthen land and natural resources governance - Through the work of PNGSL, USAID will improve the implementation of safeguards for infrastructure development; enhance the vertical and horizontal integration of participatory low-emission land use planning; and protect high carbon-density areas. .Improve the environmental sustainability of the forestry industry - USAID will increase adherence to social and environmental safeguards by forestry companies; improve implementation and coordination of sustainable forestry policies; and build capacity to enforce sustainable forestry policies. .Protect the natural resource management rights of communities - USAID will increase the capacity of rural communities to protect land and forest resource rights; improve the financial literacy and business acumen of forest owners; and enhance the transparency and integrity of information on natural resources..Strengthening natural resource governance advances the vision for an open, interconnected, resilient, and secure Indo-Pacific by protecting and advancing the region's rules-based order. Promoting transparent government policies, regulations, and transactions fosters adherence to internationally accepted standards, including environmental safeguards, and mitigates the entry and actions of predatory players.

title.narrative: Actions to Support Wide-scale Interventions to Fight TB in the Philippines (ACT SWIFT)

description.narrative: Through SWIF-TB, USAID and its partners will help expand ongoing efforts of local NGOs and private sector partners in fighting TB, such as providing payment vouchers for early TB screening; utilizing advanced technologies in TB testing; enhancing the ability of health advocates to find cases and support survivors; increasing the use of TB preventive treatment; and integrating TB screening with the testing of other lung diseases, HIV, and diabetes. These efforts will help screen at least a million Filipinos for TB and ensure proper treatment of those afflicted with the disease.

title.narrative: ASEAN Inclusive Growth in ASEAN through Innovation, Trade and E-Commerce (IGNITE)

description.narrative: ASEAN-USAID IGNITE builds upon achievements of the US-ASEAN Connectivity through Trade and Investment (US-ACTI) project and provides technical assistance across three work streams: (i) Trade Facilitation; (ii) The Digital Economy; and (iii) Science, Technology, and Innovation. Through its support to the ASEAN Secretariat, ASEAN-USAID IGNITE aims to achieve the following objectives: Objective 1: Harmonized, transparent, internationally-accepted standards, rules, and procedures known to facilitate the cross-border movement of goods and services expanded while reducing non-tariff barriers to trade. Objective 2: Improved environment for increasing the availability within and among ASEAN Member States of relevant, affordable, and secure digitally-enabled services that reflect international standards and practices and facilitate e-commerce, especially for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). Obective 3: Enabling environment strengthened that provides incentives for using science, technology, and innovation to drive open and inclusive economic growth.

title.narrative: Integrated Marine Ecosystems Management in Northern Hispaniola
Manejo Integrado de Ecosistemas Marinos en el Norte de La Española

description.narrative: The Integrated Marine Ecosystems Management in Northern Hispaniola project aims to reduce local threats to biodiversity in coastal and marine ecosystems along the Haitian-Dominican Republic border in Northern Hispaniola, while minimizing economic and cultural disruption for communities that depend on those ecosystems, and ideally creating new economic opportunities for those communities..

El proyecto de Manejo Integrado de Ecosistemas Marinos en el Norte de La Española tiene como objetivo reducir las amenazas locales a la biodiversidad en los ecosistemas costeros y marinos a lo largo de la frontera entre Haití y la República Dominicana en el Norte de La Española, minimizando al mismo tiempo la perturbación económica y cultural para las comunidades que dependen de esos ecosistemas e idealmente creando nuevas oportunidades económicas para esas comunidades..

Mecanismo de Monitoreo, Evaluación y Aprendizaje (MEL)
Mecanismo de Monitoreo, Evaluación y Aprendizaje (MEL)

description.narrative: (El Salvador): The Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) activity provides an umbrella mechanism instrument through which the USAID/El Salvador and Central America & Mexico Regional Mission, other USAID bilateral missions in the region, and USAID/Washington-based Bureaus and Offices in Central America can request MEL, knowledge management, and geographic information systems support services. This mechanism will measure programmatic impacts, results, and achievements; facilitate learning and adaptive management; and contract individual or longitudinal studies, analyses, and assessments on certain sectors or issues relevant to programs for bilateral and regional strategies. The expected overall result of the MEL contract is to enhance USAID's regional MEL capacity, and the use of empirical evidence for programming, learning and adapting. The MEL activity is uniquely positioned to provide these services due to the IP's extensive experience supporting USAID to effectively conduct MEL practices in support of reporting, learning and adaptive management, and institutionalizing best practices in Missions. The activity supports the ICS and RCS in their entirety by supporting USAID to effectively use data and evidence to inform and improve programming towards achievement of high level outcomes

title.narrative: HIV Sustainability and Human Rights for Central America project
Proyecto VIH Sostenibilidad y Derechos Humanos para Centroamérica

description.narrative: The HIV Sustainability and Human Rights for Central America project is a regional grant funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and the U.S. Presidents Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR). The project supports government and nongovernmental partners across Central America to achieve sustainable HIV epidemic control, while improving the human rights environment through the reduction of stigma and discrimination. The response will focus on policy-level interventions, ensuring that governments are able to credibly budget for impending decreases in donor funding and also take into account the needs and opinions of vulnerable populations when prioritizing funds. Working with diverse country stakeholders using strategic information and the principles of gender equity and human rights, the project seeks to catalyze country leadership and commitment to secure long-term financing; implement sustainable policies; and reduce stigma and discrimination against key populations in order to achieve sustainable HIV epidemic control. The HIV Sustainability and Human Rights for Central America project promotes gender equality, with specific cross-cutting focus on gender sensitivity and understanding. Along with support from key regional governments, the project will be implemented by Plan with partners Results for Development (R4D) and Internews. National implementation will be carried out according to the needs of each country, while leveraging the strength of Central American entities that support the region's efforts in order to sustain the response to control the epidemic.

El proyecto Sostenibilidad del VIH y Derechos Humanos para Centroamérica es una subvención regional financiada por la Agencia de los Estados Unidos para el Desarrollo Internacional (USAID) y el Plan de Emergencia del Presidente de los Estados Unidos para el Alivio del SIDA (PEPFAR). El proyecto apoya a socios gubernamentales y no gubernamentales en toda Centroamérica para lograr un control sostenible de la epidemia del VIH y, al mismo tiempo, mejorar el entorno de derechos humanos mediante la reducción del estigma y la discriminación. La respuesta se centrará en intervenciones a nivel de políticas, garantizando que los gobiernos puedan presupuestar de manera creíble las inminentes disminuciones en la financiación de los donantes y también tener en cuenta las necesidades y opiniones de las poblaciones vulnerables al priorizar los fondos. Al trabajar con diversas partes interesadas del país utilizando información estratégica y los principios de equidad de género y derechos humanos, el proyecto busca catalizar el liderazgo y el compromiso del país para asegurar financiamiento a largo plazo; implementar políticas sostenibles; y reducir el estigma y la discriminación contra las poblaciones clave para lograr un control sostenible de la epidemia del VIH. El proyecto Sostenibilidad del VIH y Derechos Humanos para Centroamérica promueve la igualdad de género, con un enfoque transversal específico en la sensibilidad y comprensión de género. Junto con el apoyo de gobiernos regionales clave, el proyecto será implementado por Plan con sus socios Results for Development (R4D) e Internews. La implementación nacional se realizará de acuerdo a las necesidades de cada país, aprovechando la fortaleza de las entidades centroamericanas que apoyan los esfuerzos de la región para sostener la respuesta para controlar la epidemia.

title.narrative: Guatemala - Sustainable Health, HIV, and Nutrition Response in Central America
Guatemala - Respuesta sostenible en salud, VIH y nutrición en Centroamérica
Guatemala - Respuesta sostenible en salud, VIH y nutrición en Centroamérica

description.narrative: (Guatemala): ....This activity will enhance reproductive, maternal, and child health and nutrition (RMCHN) through tailored, evidence-based interventions in Huehuetenango and Quiche. With FY 2024 funding, the activity will support the third household RMCHN survey, scheduled for 2025-2026. This survey will provide critical data on the impact of USAID health activities, including a subsample focusing on families with pregnant women. The findings will generate robust, evidence-based insights for decision-makers..To advance USAID's Localization Strategy, the activity will continue working with four local NGOs to strengthen their administrative, financial, and technical capacities. These NGOs will collaborate with the Sexual and Reproductive Health Observatory to advocate for regulatory protections of health rights for indigenous populations, including youth. Additionally, the activity will engage these NGOs to conduct a study on users' perceptions of health service quality. This study would complement the RMCHN survey by evaluating users' views on service quality and healthcare worker competencies, identifying gaps in access to and utilization of integrated health services...The activity will also continue the improvement of a knowledge management platform to facilitate streamlined access to RMCHN resources, integrating it with strategic government and NGO platforms for broader reach and impact..FY 2024 funds will also be used to provide support to the Ministry of Social Development and the Secretariat for Food Security and Nutrition. This support will include conducting a Household Social Registry or implementing other initiatives to assess socioeconomic conditions in underserved areas, enabling them to implement targeted social programs...This activity aligns with JSP 3.2, CDCS DO1-DO2, ICS 3.2, and RCS 1.3-2.3 by improving health outcomes and strengthening government service delivery. These efforts directly support the NSS by promoting sustainable development....

(Guatemala): ....Esta actividad mejorará la salud y nutrición reproductiva, materna e infantil (RMCHN) a través de intervenciones personalizadas y basadas en evidencia en Huehuetenango y Quiché. Con financiación para el año fiscal 2024, la actividad apoyará la tercera encuesta de hogares RMCHN, programada para 2025-2026. Esta encuesta proporcionará datos críticos sobre el impacto de las actividades de salud de USAID, incluida una submuestra centrada en familias con mujeres embarazadas. Los hallazgos generarán conocimientos sólidos y basados ​​en evidencia para los tomadores de decisiones. Para avanzar en la Estrategia de Localización de USAID, la actividad continuará trabajando con cuatro ONG locales para fortalecer sus capacidades administrativas, financieras y técnicas. Estas ONG colaborarán con el Observatorio de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva para abogar por protecciones regulatorias de los derechos de salud de las poblaciones indígenas, incluidos los jóvenes. Además, la actividad involucrará a estas ONG para realizar un estudio sobre las percepciones de los usuarios sobre la calidad de los servicios de salud. Este estudio complementaría la encuesta RMCHN al evaluar las opiniones de los usuarios sobre la calidad del servicio y las competencias de los trabajadores de la salud, identificando brechas en el acceso y la utilización de servicios de salud integrados... La actividad también continuará con la mejora de una plataforma de gestión del conocimiento para facilitar el acceso simplificado a los recursos de RMCHN, integrándola con plataformas estratégicas gubernamentales y de ONG para un mayor alcance e impacto... Los fondos del año fiscal 2024 también se utilizarán para brindar apoyo al Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y a la Secretaría de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición. Este apoyo incluirá la realización de un Registro Social de Hogares o la implementación de otras iniciativas para evaluar las condiciones socioeconómicas en áreas desatendidas, permitiéndoles implementar programas sociales específicos... Esta actividad se alinea con JSP 3.2, CDCS DO1-DO2, ICS 3.2 y RCS 1.3-2.3 al mejorar los resultados de salud y fortalecer la prestación de servicios gubernamentales. Estos esfuerzos apoyan directamente al SEN promoviendo el desarrollo sostenible....

(Guatemala): ....Esta actividad mejorará la salud y nutrición reproductiva, materna e infantil (RMCHN) a través de intervenciones personalizadas y basadas en evidencia en Huehuetenango y Quiché. Con financiación para el año fiscal 2024, la actividad apoyará la tercera encuesta de hogares RMCHN, programada para 2025-2026. Esta encuesta proporcionará datos críticos sobre el impacto de las actividades de salud de USAID, incluida una submuestra centrada en familias con mujeres embarazadas. Los hallazgos generarán conocimientos sólidos y basados ​​en evidencia para los tomadores de decisiones. Para avanzar en la Estrategia de Localización de USAID, la actividad continuará trabajando con cuatro ONG locales para fortalecer sus capacidades administrativas, financieras y técnicas. Estas ONG colaborarán con el Observatorio de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva para abogar por protecciones regulatorias de los derechos de salud de las poblaciones indígenas, incluidos los jóvenes. Además, la actividad involucrará a estas ONG para realizar un estudio sobre las percepciones de los usuarios sobre la calidad de los servicios de salud. Este estudio complementaría la encuesta RMCHN al evaluar las opiniones de los usuarios sobre la calidad del servicio y las competencias de los trabajadores de la salud, identificando brechas en el acceso y la utilización de servicios de salud integrados... La actividad también continuará con la mejora de una plataforma de gestión del conocimiento para facilitar el acceso simplificado a los recursos de RMCHN, integrándola con plataformas estratégicas gubernamentales y de ONG para un mayor alcance e impacto... Los fondos del año fiscal 2024 también se utilizarán para brindar apoyo al Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y a la Secretaría de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición. Este apoyo incluirá la realización de un Registro Social de Hogares o la implementación de otras iniciativas para evaluar las condiciones socioeconómicas en áreas desatendidas, permitiéndoles implementar programas sociales específicos... Esta actividad se alinea con JSP 3.2, CDCS DO1-DO2, ICS 3.2 y RCS 1.3-2.3 al mejorar los resultados de salud y fortalecer la prestación de servicios gubernamentales. Estos esfuerzos apoyan directamente al SEN promoviendo el desarrollo sostenible....

description.narrative: (Guatemala): This activity will develop, implement, learn, and lay the groundwork for a sustainable Youth Service Corps in Guatemala. The corps will improve youth's opportunities to improve their communities, leading to increased youth rootedness, resiliency, and hope...FY 2022 resources will build on an existing model that allows youth at risk of irregular migration to participate in a paid community service initiative. This program provides opportunities for youth, aged 15 to 29, to positively impact their own communities and achieve greater stability; develop social and emotional skills; and strengthen connections with their families and communities. Phase 1 of the activity focused on broad stakeholder engagement and a robust learning agenda to inform the design of the business model and standard operating procedures for a National Youth Service Corps. Community service will include activities related to key community priorities such as educational support and tutoring, climate action, food security, green jobs, health education and services, violence prevention, and other civic engagement activities. This experience will build youth's skills and provide experience in a work environment, while engaging them in being part of healing the social fabric that ties individuals to their communities and addresses root causes of migration...Phase II of the Activity is a direct response to the Central American Youth Empowerment Program/Central American Service Corp initiative directed in the FY 2022 Appropriations Bill. The activity contributes to the Young Women's Empowerment Initiative and aligns with ICS MOs 1.1, 1.2, 3.1, and 3.2, which strengthen rootedness of potential migrants and improves economic prosperity and well-being of youth. The activity is also linked to JSP Goal 3.3 and RCS Pillar 1.3..This IM will contribute to CAYEP by $2,344,215, GBV and WEE by $500,000, and Basic Education for Girls in Areas of Conflict by $368,331.

(Guatemala): Esta actividad desarrollará, implementará, aprenderá y sentará las bases para un Cuerpo de Servicio Juvenil sostenible en Guatemala. El cuerpo mejorará las oportunidades de los jóvenes para mejorar sus comunidades, lo que conducirá a un mayor arraigo, resiliencia y esperanza de los jóvenes... Los recursos del año fiscal 2022 se basarán en un modelo existente que permite a los jóvenes en riesgo de migración irregular participar en una iniciativa de servicio comunitario remunerado. Este programa brinda oportunidades para que los jóvenes, de 15 a 29 años, impacten positivamente sus propias comunidades y logren una mayor estabilidad; desarrollar habilidades sociales y emocionales; y fortalecer las conexiones con sus familias y comunidades. La fase 1 de la actividad se centró en una amplia participación de las partes interesadas y una sólida agenda de aprendizaje para informar el diseño del modelo de negocio y los procedimientos operativos estándar para un Cuerpo Nacional de Servicio Juvenil. El servicio comunitario incluirá actividades relacionadas con prioridades comunitarias clave, como apoyo educativo y tutoría, acción climática, seguridad alimentaria, empleos verdes, educación y servicios de salud, prevención de la violencia y otras actividades de participación cívica. Esta experiencia desarrollará las habilidades de los jóvenes y les brindará experiencia en un entorno laboral, al mismo tiempo que los involucrará en ser parte de la curación del tejido social que une a las personas con sus comunidades y aborda las causas fundamentales de la migración... La Fase II de la actividad es una respuesta directa a la iniciativa del Programa de Empoderamiento de la Juventud Centroamericana/Corporación de Servicios de Centroamérica dirigida en el Proyecto de Ley de Apropiaciones para el año fiscal 2022. La actividad contribuye a la Iniciativa de Empoderamiento de las Mujeres Jóvenes y se alinea con los MO 1.1, 1.2, 3.1 y 3.2 de ICS, que fortalecen el arraigo de los migrantes potenciales y mejoran la prosperidad económica y el bienestar de los jóvenes. La actividad también está vinculada al Objetivo 3.3 del JSP y al Pilar 1.3 del RCS. Este MI contribuirá a CAYEP con $2,344,215, GBV y WEE con $500,000 y a la educación básica para niñas en áreas de conflicto con $368,331.

title.narrative: Actividad de Atención y Tratamiento del VIH

description.narrative: The activity is to support El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Panama in reaching the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and AIDS (UNAIDS) 95-95-95 targets by 2030 such that 95% of people living with HIV know their HIV status, 95% of people living with HIV who know their HIV-positive status will access treatment, and 95% of people on treatment will have suppressed viral loads, resulting in epidemic control.

La actividad tiene como objetivo ayudar a El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras y Panamá a alcanzar las metas 95-95-95 del Programa Conjunto de las Naciones Unidas sobre el VIH y el SIDA (ONUSIDA) para 2030, de modo que el 95% de las personas que viven con el VIH conozcan su estado serológico, el 95% de las personas que viven con el VIH que conocen su estado serológico accedan al tratamiento y el 95% de las personas en tratamiento hayan suprimido las cargas virales, lo que resultará en el control de la epidemia.

description.narrative: (USAID South America Regional): .Tension is increasing in the Amazon between the seemingly opposing goals of biodiversity conservation and natural resource extraction and infrastructure development. Due to a lack of coherent regulatory frameworks, political will, and enforcement capacity, economic development in the Amazon region has generally resulted in the destruction and degradation of forests and waters, but these goals do not have to be at odds. Utilizing best environmental and social management practices (BMP) in the development of large-scale infrastructure and extractive industry projects (e.g., planning development around biological corridors, using new technology to conduct petroleum exploration, or burying pipelines) can drastically reduce unintended negative impacts and facilitate both economic development and environmental conservation...This activity will engage with private sector companies, regional governments, and civil society groups (particularly vulnerable indigenous populations) to foster the use of innovative BMPs in new large-scale development projects, focused on selected biodiverse landscapes in Peru, Colombia and Brazil. Geographies will be prioritized by a multi-sector advisory group, where BMPs could be adopted in infrastructure projects (e.g., roads and hydropower dams) and extractive industries (e.g,, mining and hydrocarbons). Key implementation approaches will include: engaging development champions from different sectors within existing networks; deploying quantitative tools and predictive modeling to demonstrate the effectiveness and differential impact of deploying BMPs; building strong partnerships to oversee BMP implementation at the site level; and replicating and scaling up the use of proven interventions. The implementing partner was selected through a competitive process. By addressing the conflict between conservation goals and extractive and infrastructure projects, the activity contributes to asserting U.S. leadership an

(USAID Regional América del Sur): .La tensión está aumentando en la Amazonia entre los objetivos aparentemente opuestos de conservación de la biodiversidad y la extracción de recursos naturales y el desarrollo de infraestructura. Debido a la falta de marcos regulatorios coherentes, voluntad política y capacidad de aplicación de la ley, el desarrollo económico en la región amazónica generalmente ha resultado en la destrucción y degradación de bosques y aguas, pero estos objetivos no tienen por qué estar reñidos. La utilización de las mejores prácticas de gestión ambiental y social (BMP, por sus siglas en inglés) en el desarrollo de infraestructura a gran escala y proyectos de industrias extractivas (por ejemplo, planificar el desarrollo alrededor de corredores biológicos, utilizar nuevas tecnologías para realizar exploraciones petroleras o enterrar oleoductos) puede reducir drásticamente los impactos negativos no deseados y facilitar tanto el desarrollo económico como la conservación ambiental... Esta actividad involucrará a empresas del sector privado, gobiernos regionales y grupos de la sociedad civil (particularmente poblaciones indígenas vulnerables) para fomentar el uso de BMP innovadoras en nuevos desarrollos a gran escala. proyectos, centrados en paisajes biodiversos seleccionados en Perú, Colombia y Brasil. Un grupo asesor multisectorial dará prioridad a las zonas geográficas donde las BMP podrían adoptarse en proyectos de infraestructura (por ejemplo, carreteras y represas hidroeléctricas) e industrias extractivas (por ejemplo, minería e hidrocarburos). Los enfoques clave de implementación incluirán: involucrar a defensores del desarrollo de diferentes sectores dentro de las redes existentes; desplegar herramientas cuantitativas y modelos predictivos para demostrar la eficacia y el impacto diferencial del despliegue de BMP; construir asociaciones sólidas para supervisar la implementación de BMP a nivel de sitio; y replicar y ampliar el uso de intervenciones probadas. El socio implementador fue seleccionado mediante un proceso competitivo. Al abordar el conflicto entre los objetivos de conservación y los proyectos extractivos y de infraestructura, la actividad contribuye a afirmar el liderazgo y la sostenibilidad de Estados Unidos.

description.narrative: (USAID South America Regional): .SERVIR-Amazonia, a joint global initiative between NASA and USAID, uses state-of-the-art geospatial and satellite technologies to empower authorities to track environmental changes in near real-time, evaluate the impact of climatic threats, and respond to natural disasters. The transformation of the Amazon by large-scale infrastructure and extractive activities, coupled with threats from a shifting climate, requires an immediate response to prevent and mitigate negative impacts on ecosystems and people. Responses to these threats must be based on accessible, timely, credible, and relevant scientific information about vast and remote landscapes..In response, SERVIR-Amazonia promotes collaboration among governments, universities, non-governmental organizations, community groups, and U.S. scientists to use geospatial information services to foster sustainable development across the Amazon region. SERVIR develops user-friendly geospatial tools focused on drought and fire risk, water resources, ecosystems management, and climate stress impacts. Three tools that will be fully implemented in FY21 are the Radar Mining Monitoring Tool, to monitor gold mining in the Peruvian Amazon; the Colombian Mining Monitoring tool to detect gold mining deforestation in Colombia; and the TerraOnTrack tool for early alerts of illegal timber extraction in protected areas of traditional communities in Brazil. .New tools will monitor the extent and structure of mangroves in Guyana; monitor soil fertility and degradation in Ecuador; and improve resilience to extreme hydrological events and forecast fire and drought in Peru, Colombia, and Brazil. These tools will distill complex data into digestible formats to improve decision-making for human safety and resources management. .. .

(USAID Regional América del Sur): .SERVIR-Amazonia, una iniciativa global conjunta entre la NASA y USAID, utiliza tecnologías geoespaciales y satelitales de última generación para capacitar a las autoridades para rastrear los cambios ambientales casi en tiempo real, evaluar el impacto de las amenazas climáticas y responder a los desastres naturales. La transformación de la Amazonía por la infraestructura a gran escala y las actividades extractivas, junto con las amenazas de un clima cambiante, requiere una respuesta inmediata para prevenir y mitigar los impactos negativos en los ecosistemas y las personas. Las respuestas a estas amenazas deben basarse en información científica accesible, oportuna, creíble y relevante sobre paisajes vastos y remotos. En respuesta, SERVIR-Amazonia promueve la colaboración entre gobiernos, universidades, organizaciones no gubernamentales, grupos comunitarios y científicos estadounidenses para utilizar servicios de información geoespacial para fomentar el desarrollo sostenible en toda la región amazónica. SERVIR desarrolla herramientas geoespaciales fáciles de usar centradas en el riesgo de sequías e incendios, recursos hídricos, gestión de ecosistemas e impactos del estrés climático. Tres herramientas que se implementarán por completo en el año fiscal 21 son la herramienta Radar Mining Monitoring Tool, para monitorear la minería de oro en la Amazonía peruana; la herramienta de Monitoreo Minero Colombiano para detectar la deforestación por minería aurífera en Colombia; y la herramienta TerraOnTrack para alertas tempranas de extracción ilegal de madera en áreas protegidas de comunidades tradicionales en Brasil. .Nuevas herramientas monitorearán la extensión y estructura de los manglares en Guyana; monitorear la fertilidad y degradación del suelo en Ecuador; y mejorar la resiliencia ante eventos hidrológicos extremos y pronosticar incendios y sequías en Perú, Colombia y Brasil. Estas herramientas sintetizarán datos complejos en formatos digeribles para mejorar la toma de decisiones para la seguridad humana y la gestión de recursos. ...

description.narrative: (USAID South America Regional): AIRR aims to strengthen the engagement of indigenous peoples in the conservation of biodiversity in the Amazon, through sustainable economic development and reduced forest loss on indigenous lands. This will be achieved through two complementary approaches: Indigenous rights and economic interests incorporated into private and public sector development planning; and Indigenous enterprises equitably and sustainably scaled to regional and global markets. The project works with the regional federation of the Amazon (COICA), and with the national indigenous federations of Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana and Suriname. The governance of the project includes regional, national, and economic Steering Committees composed of representatives of the partner indigenous organizations. The project supports the participation of indigenous federations in international consultation processes such as COP27 Climate Change Conference, second COP of Escazu agreement, United Nations Universal Periodic Review, Convention on Biological Diversity in China. With FY 2022 funds, AIRR will continue strengthening capacities in leadership, advocacy, negotiations and dialogue and to monitor deforestation and other environmental crimes. This work allows for better representation when addressing territorial rights. Gender and youth considerations are present in all AIRR activities, but a more structured Gender and Youth Plan has recently begun implementation in earnest. A total of 29 indigenous enterprises in Colombia, Peru, Brazil and Ecuador will be supported with FY 2022 funds. USAID will provide advisory services in business, financial, technical, environmental and social services. The objective is to improve the indigenous enterprises, according to the needs determined in the investment memorandums and environmental monitoring plans. Activities include work on agroforestry, tourism, agribusiness, sustainable fisheries and aquaculture, and timber and non-

(USAID Regional América del Sur): AIRR tiene como objetivo fortalecer el compromiso de los pueblos indígenas en la conservación de la biodiversidad en la Amazonia, a través del desarrollo económico sostenible y la reducción de la pérdida de bosques en tierras indígenas. Esto se logrará mediante dos enfoques complementarios: los derechos e intereses económicos indígenas incorporados en la planificación del desarrollo de los sectores público y privado; y empresas indígenas escaladas de manera equitativa y sostenible a los mercados regionales y globales. El proyecto trabaja con la federación regional de la Amazonía (COICA), y con las federaciones nacionales indígenas de Brasil, Perú, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana y Surinam. La gobernanza del proyecto incluye comités directivos regionales, nacionales y económicos compuestos por representantes de las organizaciones indígenas socias. El proyecto apoya la participación de federaciones indígenas en procesos de consulta internacional como la Conferencia de Cambio Climático COP27, segunda COP del acuerdo de Escazú, Examen Periódico Universal de las Naciones Unidas, Convenio sobre la Diversidad Biológica en China. Con fondos del año fiscal 2022, AIRR continuará fortaleciendo capacidades en liderazgo, promoción, negociación y diálogo y para monitorear la deforestación y otros delitos ambientales. Este trabajo permite una mejor representación a la hora de abordar los derechos territoriales. Las consideraciones de género y juventud están presentes en todas las actividades de AIRR, pero recientemente se ha comenzado a implementar seriamente un Plan de Género y Juventud más estructurado. Un total de 29 empresas indígenas en Colombia, Perú, Brasil y Ecuador recibirán apoyo con fondos del año fiscal 2022. USAID brindará servicios de asesoría en servicios comerciales, financieros, técnicos, ambientales y sociales. El objetivo es mejorar las empresas indígenas, de acuerdo con las necesidades determinadas en los memorandos de inversión y planes de seguimiento ambiental. title.narrative: Economic & Financial Inclusion to Drive Entrepreneurship and Employment (FIDEE)
Inclusión Económica y Financiera para Impulsar el Emprendimiento y el Empleo (FIDEE)
Inclusión Económica y Financiera para Impulsar el Emprendimiento y el Empleo (FIDEE)

description.narrative: (USAID South America Regional): Fleeing the socio-economic and political crisis in Venezuela, more than five million migrants and refugees currently shelter outside of their country and the number is rising. This includes more than one million Venezuelans in Peru and more than 400,000 in Ecuador. Upon arriving in their new host countries, migrants first and foremost need a livelihood to sustain themselves and their families and begin to integrate and contribute to their new communities. USAID implements this activity to provide targeted assistance supporting the long-term, economic integration of Venezuelans in the countries of Peru and Ecuador. The activity is focused on programs on employment, entrepreneurship, and financial inclusion. With FY 2022 funds, USAID will continue to help Venezuelans and locals to improve their overall economic well-being. This will be accomplished through: intensive entrepreneurship and small business development training programs, including access to seed capital; support for labor market insertion through training and skills development, job matching, and private sector outreach; and, increased access to financial services, including savings, credit and insurance products, through partnerships with financial institutions, particularly credit unions. Taking into account the distinct challenges that women face in their pursuit of an economic livelihood, with FY 2022 funds, USAID will continue specific interventions to support women at risk of or facing gender-based violence (GBV) to help reduce violence against women and enable their participation in economic activities as an element of their and their families inclusion in their new communities. By contributing to women's economic empowerment, their vulnerability and susceptibility to GBV are reduced. The activity will also work with men in the context of these livelihood interventions and will seek to impart healthy models of masculinity, including the role of both men and women a

(USAID Regional América del Sur): Huyendo de la crisis socioeconómica y política en Venezuela, más de cinco millones de migrantes y refugiados actualmente se refugian fuera de su país y el número va en aumento. Esto incluye a más de un millón de venezolanos en Perú y más de 400.000 en Ecuador. Al llegar a sus nuevos países de acogida, los migrantes necesitan ante todo un medio de vida para mantenerse a sí mismos y a sus familias y comenzar a integrarse y contribuir a sus nuevas comunidades. USAID implementa esta actividad para brindar asistencia específica que apoye la integración económica a largo plazo de los venezolanos en los países de Perú y Ecuador. La actividad se centra en programas sobre empleo, emprendimiento e inclusión financiera. Con los fondos del año fiscal 2022, USAID continuará ayudando a los venezolanos y locales a mejorar su bienestar económico general. Esto se logrará mediante: programas intensivos de capacitación en emprendimiento y desarrollo de pequeñas empresas, incluido el acceso a capital inicial; apoyo a la inserción en el mercado laboral mediante capacitación y desarrollo de habilidades, búsqueda de empleo y extensión al sector privado; y un mayor acceso a los servicios financieros, incluidos productos de ahorro, crédito y seguros, a través de asociaciones con instituciones financieras, en particular cooperativas de crédito. Teniendo en cuenta los distintos desafíos que enfrentan las mujeres en su búsqueda de un medio de vida económico, con fondos del año fiscal 2022, USAID continuará con intervenciones específicas para apoyar a las mujeres en riesgo o que enfrentan violencia de género (VBG) para ayudar a reducir la violencia contra las mujeres y permitir su participación en actividades económicas como un elemento de su inclusión y la de sus familias en sus nuevas comunidades. Al contribuir al empoderamiento económico de las mujeres, se reduce su vulnerabilidad y susceptibilidad a la violencia de género. La actividad también trabajará con hombres en el contexto de estas intervenciones de medios de vida y buscará impartir modelos saludables de masculinidad, incluido el papel tanto de hombres como de mujeres.

title.narrative: Respuesta comunitaria a los crímenes contra la conservación

description.narrative: (USAID South America Regional): In response to key threats posed by transnational conservation crimes affecting the Peruvian Amazon: wildlife trafficking, IUU fisheries, illegal mining and deforestation, USAID program apply a "whole-of-Amazon" systems approach to improve the capacity and collaboration of civil society networks and the private sector across the region. Through this approach, the activity seeks to decrease the ease and profit of engaging in illicit actions by reducing demand for illegal products, increasing public awareness, developing private sector partnerships, strengthening capacities of media outlets and journalist networks to improve reporting on wildlife trafficking and sustainable solutions for the Amazon, and providing community stewards with the tools to defend biodiversity. With FY 2022 funds, it will support the Citizen Science for the Amazon Network for improved fisheries monitoring, and design and start implementation of a coordinated regional action plan to improve fisheries monitoring in priority transnational basins. The activity will also design and implement a solution search contest, based on best practices in reducing conservation crimes. The contest will identify, reward, and spotlight what is already working in conservation and development. Additionally, the activity will work with strategic private stakeholders (e.g., transport companies and extractive industries operating in the Western Amazon) to help them understand the negative effects of conservation crimes, and specifically negative effects on their business models. This will be accomplished through campaigns, workshops, among other related activities. The project will also help private stakeholders to find solutions to address conservation crimes in their businesses or industries by making assessments and analysis (e.g., on supply chain risks), providing technical information and advice, and by developing or promoting best practices, standards, and specialized conferenc

(USAID Regional América del Sur): En respuesta a las principales amenazas planteadas por los crímenes de conservación transnacionales que afectan la Amazonía peruana: tráfico de vida silvestre, pesca INDNR, minería ilegal y deforestación, el programa de USAID aplica un enfoque de sistemas "toda la Amazonía" para mejorar la capacidad y la colaboración de las redes de la sociedad civil y el sector privado en toda la región. A través de este enfoque, la actividad busca disminuir la facilidad y las ganancias de participar en acciones ilícitas al reducir la demanda de productos ilegales, aumentar la conciencia pública, desarrollar asociaciones con el sector privado, fortalecer las capacidades de los medios de comunicación y las redes de periodistas para mejorar la información sobre el tráfico de vida silvestre y las soluciones sostenibles para la Amazonía, y brindar a los administradores comunitarios las herramientas para defender la biodiversidad. Con fondos del año fiscal 2022, apoyará la Red de Ciencia Ciudadana para la Amazonía para mejorar el monitoreo de la pesca, y diseñará e iniciará la implementación de un plan de acción regional coordinado para mejorar el monitoreo de la pesca en cuencas transnacionales prioritarias. La actividad también diseñará e implementará un concurso de búsqueda de soluciones, basado en mejores prácticas para reducir los delitos de conservación. El concurso identificará, recompensará y destacará lo que ya está funcionando en conservación y desarrollo. Además, la actividad trabajará con actores privados estratégicos (por ejemplo, empresas de transporte e industrias extractivas que operan en la Amazonía occidental) para ayudarlos a comprender los efectos negativos de los delitos de conservación y, específicamente, los efectos negativos en sus modelos de negocios. Esto se logrará a través de campañas, talleres, entre otras actividades relacionadas. El proyecto también ayudará a las partes interesadas privadas a encontrar soluciones para abordar los delitos de conservación en sus negocios o industrias mediante la realización de evaluaciones y análisis (por ejemplo, sobre riesgos de la cadena de suministro), proporcionando información y asesoramiento técnicos, y desarrollando o promoviendo mejores prácticas, estándares y conferencias especializadas.
