description.narrative: (USAID South America Regional): .The eastern Pacific is among the world's richest fisheries. The ecological impact of distant water fleets brings increased international attention to the challenges of illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and the operations of these fleets frequently associated with corruption. Addressing IUU is critical for both biodiversity protection and livelihoods and food security of coastal communities. ..The partnership between NOAA and USAID aims to improve law enforcement capabilities in Ecuador, Peru and Colombia, improving the coordination on IUU and overfishing across the region. Under Component 1, NOAA will support regulators to identify and fight against IUU fishing and to advance implementation of the Port States Measurement Agreement (PSMA). Component 2 aims to improve management of fisheries and marine protected areas. This activity supports the Maritime SAFE Act (2019) and complements the efforts of the Mission to address climate change in marine ecosystems and promote biodiversity conservation of marine flora and fauna...With FY 2022 funding, NOAA will continue building the capacity of port inspectors to detect illegal fish catches, and strengthen the political will to implement Port States Measure Agreements (PSMA), via workshops, training, and ad hoc coaching. NOAA also plans to ramp up interventions in support of the governments of Colombia and Ecuador to manage and enforce new restrictions around the Eastern Tropical Pacific Marine Corridor, a planned marine protected area with extremely high biodiversity, currently under threat from overfishing and other commercial activities. Peru will also benefit from these set of interventions as observers, to improve their management of marine protected areas within their waters. Finally, the program will work with the governments of Peru and Ecuador to strengthen international agreements to manage deep-water fisheries. .. .

Conservar la biodiversidad y gestionar los recursos naturales de manera que mantengan su viabilidad a largo plazo y preserven su potencial para satisfacer las necesidades de las generaciones presentes y futuras. Las actividades incluyen la lucha contra la explotación ilegal y corrupta de los recursos naturales y el control de especies invasoras. Los programas en este elemento deben integrarse con el Área de Agricultura bajo el Área de Crecimiento Económico y Mitigación de Conflictos y Reconciliación bajo la Categoría de Paz y Seguridad, cuando sea aplicable y apropiado.

title.narrative: Partnership to combat illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing in Peru and Ecuador
Lucha contra la pesca INDNR en Perú y Ecuador (Por La Pesca)

description.narrative: the purpose of this activity is to reduce illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing by national and foreign fleets in four socio-economically and ecologically important artisanal fisheries.

(USAID Regional América del Sur): La pesca ilegal, no declarada y no reglamentada (INDNR) está impulsada por capacidades organizativas deficientes de las organizaciones de pescadores, mala gobernanza en múltiples niveles e incentivos insuficientes para prácticas de pesca formales y responsables, lo que amenaza la sostenibilidad de las pesquerías artesanales objetivo (calamar gigante, dorado, atún y pulpo) y la biodiversidad asociada, así como los medios de vida y la resiliencia de las comunidades costeras. En las pesquerías artesanales seleccionadas, esta actividad abordará la pesca INDNR mediante: 1) la promoción del intercambio de datos y la transparencia para la toma de decisiones, junto con la promoción de una regulación y gestión participativa y basada en la ciencia de las cuatro pesquerías; 2) Formalización de los pescadores y sus organizaciones; 3) Desarrollo organizacional y creación de capacidad para las organizaciones de pescadores y sus miembros, así como para otros actores clave de la cadena de valor; y 4) generar influencia de mercado y financiación para la pesca formal y sostenible. El acuerdo de adjudicación se firmó el 21 de septiembre de 2022.

description.narrative: (Barbados and Eastern Caribbean): The CBEE-R activity will support ESC governments and private sector stakeholders to strengthen legal and regulatory structures in specific areas, build institutional capacity to properly implement business reforms, and facilitate public-private dialogue to define and support reform priorities and initiatives. An assessment of the unique situation in each country will be done prior to implementation of the activity. It will be implemented in two phases. Phase one will include Guyana, Suriname, Saint Lucia, and Grenada, while phase two will focus on Barbados, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Dominica, and St. Kitts and Nevis...Significantly constrained economic growth across the ESC has created the circumstances for unsustainable high public borrowing. There is a need for businesses and governments in the region to undertake reforms that will catalyze economic growth while simultaneously building resilience to disasters and improving risk mitigation in order to create sustainable, strong Caribbean economies...CBEE-R will improve services under five components: Electricity, Connectivity and Digital Economy, Digital Financial Services, Access to Finance, and Informality. Each of the sectors will be strengthened by introducing approaches to eliminate or reduce current bottlenecks or require upgraded systems. Under a sixth focus area, the activity will build the capacity of key stakeholders to support the development of a strong mechanism for public-private dialogue. By combining all approaches, CBEE-R will improve the regional environment for businesses to develop and thrive, promoting economic growth for each of the ESC countries involved and the overall Caribbean region. This activity will support USAID/ESC Mission's objective to promote a safe, prosperous, and resilient Caribbean region that promotes accountable institutions, economic development, and private sector-led growth, all in support of the Agency's Private Sector Engagement

description.narrative: (State Western Hemisphere Regional): .CariSECURE 2.0 builds upon the successes and lessons learned from CariSECURE, both implemented by the United Nations Development Programme. CariSECURE 2.0 seeks to reduce youth involvement in crime and violence and strengthen counter TIP efforts in the Caribbean. It uses a multi-pronged, human rights-based approach designed to improve national capacities to use evidence-based approaches to identify the root causes of youth crime and design policies, strategies, programs, and interventions...While there is a dearth of timely, disaggregated, and comprehensive youth crime data, evidence suggests youth are both the greatest perpetrators and victims of violent crimes in the region. Moreover, TIP appears to be increasing in prevalence in the Caribbean, most recently linked to the crisis of forced out-migration from Venezuela. While the paucity of reliable, timely, and comparable data is also present regarding human trafficking, anecdotal evidence suggests that youth are among the most impacted by these crimes...FY 2022 funding will support activities at the regional, national, and community levels in the EC to build the capacity of youth-serving institutions in Barbados, Grenada, and St. Vincent and the Grenadines to better collect, analyze, and use timely, reliable, and standardized disaggregated data for youth crime prevention and response. Funding will also bolster state capacity to identify, screen, investigate, and prosecute trafficking cases and provide resources and technical support to Barbados, Trinidad and Tobago, Saint Lucia, and Antigua and Barbuda...This activity supports both the Regional Development Cooperation Strategy, relevant ICS, and USAID's localization priorities through partnering with local and regional partners. It also works to build the assets, agency, and enabling environment of youth in line with PYD and implements work towards the Youth Policy's three objectives of access, participation, and system

title.narrative: New Community Based Countering Wildlife Trafficking

description.narrative: (USAID Central Africa Regional): USAID will use FY 2022 Biodiversity funds on technical assistance, community outreach, and provision of materials to establish measures in the landscape encompassing the Garamba, Bili-Uele, and Chinko protected areas to dissuade poaching and combat wildlife trafficking in the border region between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Central African Republic. This activity will enable communities surrounding protected areas to safely pursue pro-conservation livelihoods and meet basic needs in a secure manner. The activity will demonstrate an inclusive approach to community resilience to insecurity, alleviating key threats to biodiversity, the bushmeat and wildlife trade and trafficking, taking into consideration cultural, livelihood and food security...This activity will contribute to advancing U.S. government priorities in Central Africa designed to maintain the ecological integrity of the humid forest ecosystem of the Congo Basin, which is vital to regional stability, and a U.S. foreign policy priority. It contributes to Joint Strategic Plan Strategic Objective 2.2: (Promote healthy, educated and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives) by protecting natural resources critical to long term, sustainable growth, and food and water security..

title.narrative: USAID - Forestry and Biodiversity Support Activity (FABS)

description.narrative: (USAID Central Africa Regional): USAID will use FY 2022 Biodiversity and Sustainable Landscapes funds to address threats to biodiversity conservation and sound forest management in the Congo Basin. USAID's Forestry and Biodiversity Support activity will build the capacity of targeted ministries and regional platforms to understand and address local threats to the environment. It will include a small grants component, catalyze private sector investment in "green enterprises," develop civil society organizations' capacity to implement their own solutions and advocate for greater accountability of government, build capacity of government agencies to formulate and implement policies, and ensure lessons learned are institutionalized within Central Africa. The activity will integrate gender and vulnerable peoples' considerations into grants, capacity-building, policy analysis, and advocacy...This activity will contribute to advancing the U.S. government priority of regional stability in Central Africa by maintaining the ecological integrity of humid forests of the Congo Basin. It contributes to Joint Strategic Plan Strategic Objective 2.2: (Promote healthy, educated and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives) by protecting natural resources critical to long term growth, food, and water security. The activity will build capacity of regional governments to meet Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Climate Agreement and access global climate financing through the Green Climate Fund and Central African Forest Initiative, while catalyzing private sector investment in low emission development. This activity will contribute to combating wildlife trafficking by strengthening the capacity of law enforcement agencies and empowering civil society organizations to hold them responsible for implementing wildlife laws..

title.narrative: EPP - Building effective management and sustainable financing for the Okapi Wildlife Reserve through a Public-Private partnership - WCS

description.narrative: (USAID Central Africa Regional): .USAID FY 2022 funds will be used to support the implementation of a public-private partnership agreement signed between the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) and the Congolese Institute for the Conservation of Nature to protect the resources of the Okapi Wildlife Reserve. This reserve hosts large blocks of intact forest and important populations of large mammals, including the okapi. The okapi are only found in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the species is confirmed to be endangered. The primary objective of this agreement is to establish long-term management of this important protected area, leverage substantial private financial and technical resources from outside the country to build the capacity of park management at the local and national level. This activity will also build the constituency around this protected area and contribute to advancing CARPE's Strategy designed to maintain forest ecosystem functions of the Congo Basin and contribute to human well-being, which is vital to greater regional stability, a U.S. foreign policy priority...This activity will contribute to advancing the U.S. government's priorities in Central Africa designed to maintain the ecological integrity of the humid forest ecosystem of the Congo Basin, which is vital to regional stability, a U.S. foreign policy priority. It contributes to Joint Strategic Plan Strategic Objective 2.2: (Promote healthy, educated and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives) by protecting natural resources critical to long term, sustainable growth, and food and water security..

description.narrative: Entrusting the management of tropical forests to the people who live in and depend on them is the fairest and most effective means of protecting them. However, until recently, communities in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) had no possibility of securing legal rights to their rainforest home. Building on the passage of landmark community forest legislation, this project aims to lay the foundations for community-based forest management in DRC, by empowering local and indigenous communities to secure their rights and thrive through sustainable livelihoods. We will do this by piloting innovative livelihoods, supporting traditional and inclusive governance of forests, and strengthening the institutions, policies, and know-how necessary to mainstream this approach. Community forests to drive improved livelihoods and wellbeing in forest communities, as well as biodiversity protection and reduced deforestation in target areas in DRC, providing a scalable model by 2025 for nationwide implementation.

description.narrative: (USAID Central Africa Regional): USAID's Shade-grown Cocoa Activity will establish employment opportunities for local populations, sound management of primary and secondary forests, and decrease deforestation pressure for extractive uses of forests. The activity will 1) establish and strengthen networks of cocoa producers to improve the quality, quantity and sustainability of their cocoa; 2) establish and strengthen linkages with all stages in the cocoa value chain as a sustainable, forest-friendly export crop; 3) strengthen enabling conditions needed for the success of the cocoa value chain; and 4) increase revenue and non-revenue benefits of stakeholder farmers. USAID intends to leverage, at a minimum, matching funds from the private sector. While the "focused" Sustainable Landscape funds will be used primarily to alleviate the pressure of deforestation, they will indirectly contribute to biodiversity outcomes by protecting forest habitat and key biodiversity species in these important forests. By demonstrating an effective approach to reducing deforestation, they will also assist the government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Climate Agreement..This activity will contribute to advancing U.S. government priorities in Central Africa designed to maintain the ecological integrity of the humid forest ecosystem of the Congo Basin, which is vital to regional stability, a U.S. foreign policy priority. It contributes to Joint Strategic Plan Strategic Objective 2.2: (Promote healthy, educated and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives) by protecting natural resources critical to long term, sustainable growth, and food and water security. This activity will support the implementation of USAID's Private Sector Engagement Strategy as well as the Climate Strategy... .

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

description.narrative: Under each PPII award, the recipient (who also serves as the fund manager) will create a private equity investment fund with a ten-year life specifically targeting SMEs. Each investment fund will be capitalized using USAID grant contributions, a small contribution from the recipient, and contributions from other investors to include potentially the private sector and/or donors and development finance institutions. Each PPII award recipient is required to secure investors to match the USAID contribution on at least a 1:1 basis.

title.narrative: OEGI- LMS-Regional Resilience Learning Associate Award

description.narrative: (USAID East Africa Regional): Using FY 2022 funds, USAID/Kenya and East Africa (KEA) will continue the implementation of a demand-driven regional learning agenda activity to ensure that resilience interventions are based on evidence and appropriate to the regional context. The Resilience Learning Activity (RLA) will continue its work to facilitate more responsive and geographically customized analytics through meta-analysis of data across targeted East African stakeholders. To increase analytical capacities, RLA will organize regional virtual data analytics training, building on the Horn of Africa Resilience Network (HoRN) learning sessions conducted in 2022, and will launch a community of practice with a group of professionals who will use data analytics, monitoring, and evaluation for evidence-based decision making to improve regional resilience against recurrent shocks and stresses. .The Resilience Learning Activity (RLA) is aligned with USAID's goals and the Horn of Africa (HOA) Resilience Framework. It strengthens capacities for analytics in resilience, facilitates learning for adaptive management, and improves knowledge management and communication. .RLA is co-funded by the Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance, USAID/Somalia, and the USAID/KEA operating units which support local, regional, and national organizations and institutions in the HOA. RLA will contribute to USAID/KEA being a center for excellence in resilience programming via coordination and leveraging cross-learning in the HOA region across six USAID resilience focus countries... .

description.narrative: (Kenya): The long-term sustainability of USAID development assistance requires local ownership and strengthened capacity of local organizations and governments; strong local leadership; empowered communities with the ability to advocate for their needs; and systems in place that produce sustainable development outcomes at the national, county, sub-county, and community levels. Using FY 2019 funds, USAID will provide organizational development and capacity-building technical assistance to strengthen the role and capacity of local development organizations, local Kenyan entities, and local governments. This will foster locally led development and implementation of sustainable development programs in support of U.S. government priorities on supporting Kenya on its journey to self-reliance towards a time when foreign assistance will no longer be necessary. USAID support to Kenyan local private, public, and civil society sectors will help establish county-wide umbrella organizations that will draw on expertise and resources to foster community-led, -managed and -owned development. Through co-creation, USAID will work with these local entities to accelerate county-level self-reliance by identifying and addressing development priorities and challenges. The FY 2019 funds will also support the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief and the Office of the U.S. Global AIDS Coordinator's mandate towards at least 70 percent of PEPFAR awards transitioned to local partners by September 2020. This activity also demonstrates unique American leadership and will help transition Kenya from an aid recipient country to an economic partner, a key goal under the Administration priorities and the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan....

title.narrative: Mission Support for Journey to Self-Reliance Pivot(MSP)

description.narrative: (Kenya): The purpose of the Mission Support for Journey to Self-Reliance Pivot (MSP) is to support USAID/Kenya and East Africa (KEA) staff and stakeholders (e.g. local and national governments, local and regional partners) to be more efficient, effective, transparent and skilled in achieving development outcomes through strategic design, performance management, Collaborating Learning and Adapting (CLA), organizational development to enable the Mission advance regional and national journeys to self-reliance (J2SR). MSP equips the Mission to advance the regional and national J2SR by: Providing training on various aspects of the program cycle,supporting the Missions design work,organizing and positioning Missions teams and offices for optimal functionality and providing evidence for decision making..USAID/KEA seeks to advance J2SR for Kenya and the region through its programming and collaboration with local stakeholders. MSP's mandate includes championing the J2SR, providing products and support to advance J2SR among Mission staff and stakeholders, equip staff with knowledge and skills as well as ensuring functional organizational structures.Apart from capacity building and organizational development at the team, office and Mission levels, MSP is also promoting the use of primary metrics, secondary and custom J2SR indicators. MSP oversaw the development of memorandum of understanding with counties to enhance collaboration on common programming areas and to enable counties to take up more of a role in planning, financing and implementing programs to meet their developmental needs. These efforts help local governments to strengthen their effectiveness and sustainability leading to a more stable and prosperous U.S. partner.

title.narrative: OEGI - Kenya County Small Business Centers Program

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2022 Feed the Future funds, USAID will continue its support for the Kenya Small Business Development Centers (SBDC) activity to strengthen Kenya's private sector competitiveness and enhance its prospects for sustained growth by increasing the quality, quantity and sustainability of Kenya's SBDCs. The activity will work to establish a network of six SBDCs, which will provide an array of services to micro and small businesses, including; business advisory services, trade and market information, facilitating access to finance, and sharing policy innovations. This will increase the productivity and profitability of micro and small businesses through tailored advisory and consulting services and catalyze the growth and competitiveness in the domestic, regional and international markets..The activity will also help the Kenyan private sector advocate for a conducive business environment by supporting sectoral Business Associations (BAs) which will advocate for their members. These BAs will focus on analyzing and advocating for an enabling business and investment environment on behalf of their members through Public-Private Dialogue. .The activity will also support agriculture Business Associations (BAs) at the county and national levels with a focus on market systems strengthening and producing value addition. Specifically, the activity will enhance the BAs' capacity to analyze policies and advocate for a positive business environment. By strengthening BAs'management capacity, technical skills, resource mobilization, member participation, and external engagement ability, USAID will also enable BA members to be vibrant and competitive by increasing investments, creating jobs, and growing businesses that can create jobs and reduce poverty.. ..

description.narrative: (USAID Africa Regional): The Regional Leadership Center East Africa (RLC East Africa) is a program under the Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI). RLC East Africa is located on the campus of Kenyatta University in Nairobi, Kenya and provides leadership training, networking, and professional development activities to young people ages 18-35 in East Africa (Burundi, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of Congo, Republic of Congo, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda)...USAID AFR Regional FY 2022 funds will support RLC East Africa efforts to help to build the skills of young African women and men in the public, private, and civic sectors and serves as a platform for regional collaboration driven by young leaders.

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): .The PSE Kenya Bilateral mechanism will leverage funding from Grand Challenges Canada and other donors to support strengthening Investment Readiness programs (IRPs) for health in Africa. The expected amount to be leveraged is approximately $1.5 M Canadian dollars. These funds will support a network of select IRPs in Africa by enabling to work more closely with potential investors, experimenting with alternative IRP models (e.g., venture studios instead of traditional accelerators) and incentivizing health-specific considerations through targeted technical assistance. .The objective is for IRPs to increase the likelihood of investment readiness among health innovators to attract investors. This work supports scaling of health innovations through an ecosystem (vs. individual company) focus. This builds on recommendations from an IRP landscape analysis in Africa report that USAID and GCC conducted which found that existing IRPs in Africa (publication imminent) lack a focus on health, have limited engagement with early stage investors and need tailored support to be more efficient. This activity will enable CII achieve its localization targets as the mechanism being used is a local bilateral mechanism. It also will enable the development of the IRP ecosystem by supporting the capacity of IRP providers which will increase the number of individuals with technical expertise in investment readiness.

title.narrative: SPA- Cost Reimbursable Contract: Development Outreach and Communication (DOC) Support to KEA

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Development Outreach and Communication (DOC) Support activity provides the Mission with a wide range of communications and outreach services. In Kenya, the activity is contributing to the mission's overarching communications objective: to increase strategic engagement with KEA target audiences in support of Kenya's Journey to Self-Reliance (J2SR). ..DOC plays a key role in developing and implementing USAID KEA's multi-year communications strategy. The results-based approach aims to engage and empower staff and implementing partners, increase the number of Kenyan voices engaged in a national dialogue on development and the use of evidence and data in communications-related decision making. The activity infuses a private sector lens on development and organizational communications practices and often partners with Kenyan firms' private sector to research or deliver compelling messages to local communities. DOC creates relevant, impactful, and high-quality visual and written content that highlight the U.S. tax payers dollars that produce real-life impact in the lives of Kenyans. .The importance of DOC's activities include effective communications and outreach, delivering information to audiences. As a result, it builds greater understanding of USAID's investments, and ensure that local voices and perspectives inform development programs and their objectives. The project contributes to the mission's overarching communications objective to increase strategic engagement with key target audiences in support of Kenya's Journey to Self-Reliance (J2SR) and the Mission's development objectives through focused, targeted communications and outreach.

description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): Despite challenges in the delivery of Family Planning (FP) services during the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent military coup in Burkina Faso, USAID's flagship FP activity continues to adapt and catalyze pathways to scaling up FP High Impact Practices (HIPs) in Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger and Togo. HIPs are critical to enabling countries to achieve their ambitious country-level FP goals and advancing the 2030 Ouagadougou Partnership (OP) and FP2030 targets. The OP's goal of adding 2.2 million additional FP users in the nine OP countries by 2020 was exceeded and a new ambitious target has been set to double the number of users of modern contraceptives to reach 13 million additional users by 2030. FY 2022 activities include using previous year funds to:.Conduct supportive supervision of public and non-governmental health facilities in offering FP, MCH and nutrition and integration of FP to the other maternal and child health services.Ensure the provision of essential medical equipment to selected public and non-governmental health facilities to improve quality of FP and MCH service delivery.Expand youth-led and youth-specific FP/RH activities in the 23 intervention districts.Engage and leverage domestic, donor, and West African communities and resources to build sustainability and scale of selected HIPs.Institutionalize a sustainable and self-regulating system of quality assurance. Collaborate and coordinate with other USAID FP/RH partners working on commodity security, demand creation, policy, learning, and related health systems.It will support the provision of comprehensive voluntary FP services closer to where people live in urban and peri-urban areas through facility-based, outreach mobile clinics and community based distribution of commodities. This strategy helps to reduce travel by patients to health centers thereby reducing carbon footprint from travel and help mitigate the climate impact of project activities...

title.narrative: Peace through Evaluation, Learning, and Adapting (PELA)
La paix par l'évaluation, l'apprentissage et l'adaptation (PELA)

description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): USAID will continue to fund its evaluation, learning, and knowledge management platform that informs USAID's broader countering violent extremism (CVE) and conflict prevention efforts in West Africa. FY 2019 activities will include:Analyzing the specific drivers of violent extremism (VE) in targeted geographic locations.Assessing emerging methods of measuring project performance in high threat environment.Evaluating USAID peacebuilding and CVE interventions.Organizing regional learning events to improve and educate CVE and peacebuilding practitioners.Implementing and regularly updating USAID's West Africa's CVE and conflict mitigation learning agenda..Evaluation, learning, and knowledge management platforms are essential to USAID's commitment to rigorous evaluation and data-driven decision making. PELA provides high-quality information and learning products to regional, governmental, and civil society actors through desk and field research, activity evaluations, and facilitation of learning events. This activity builds the capacity of local actors to manage their own CVE responses and ultimately advances countries on their journey to self-reliance by expanding the CVE knowledge base. This flexible activity will support programming in West Africa as new VEO threats are identified..PELA ensures effectiveness for the U.S. taxpayer by ensuring that USAID CVE programming is informed by high-quality evidence, and ultimately defends U.S. national security by facilitating learning aimed to stop the spread of violent extremist groups that threaten U.S. interests. This activity contributes directly to JSP Strategic Objectives 1.2 (Defeat ISIS, al-Qa'ida and other transnational terrorist organizations, and counter state-sponsored, regional, and local terrorist groups that threaten U.S. national security interests) and 4.1 (Strengthen the effectiveness and sustainability of our diplomacy and development investments).

description.narrative: Enhancing Growth through Regional Agricultural Input Systems(ENGRAIS) will expand the supply of quality fertilizer for improved food security in West Africa.

(USAID Région Afrique de l'Ouest) : L'USAID continuera de financer sa plateforme d'évaluation, d'apprentissage et de gestion des connaissances qui éclaire les efforts plus larges de l'USAID en matière de lutte contre l'extrémisme violent (CVE) et de prévention des conflits en Afrique de l'Ouest. Les activités de l'exercice 2019 comprendront : L'analyse des facteurs spécifiques de l'extrémisme violent (EV) dans des zones géographiques ciblées. L'évaluation des méthodes émergentes de mesure des performances des projets dans un environnement à forte menace. L'évaluation des interventions de consolidation de la paix et de CVE de l'USAID. à une évaluation rigoureuse et à une prise de décision fondée sur les données. PELA fournit des informations et des produits d'apprentissage de haute qualité aux acteurs régionaux, gouvernementaux et de la société civile par le biais de recherches documentaires et sur le terrain, d'évaluations d'activités et de facilitation d'événements d'apprentissage. Cette activité renforce la capacité des acteurs locaux à gérer leurs propres réponses CVE et, en fin de compte, fait progresser les pays sur leur chemin vers l'autonomie en élargissant la base de connaissances CVE. Cette activité flexible soutiendra la programmation en Afrique de l'Ouest à mesure que de nouvelles menaces VEO sont identifiées. PELA garantit l'efficacité pour le contribuable américain en garantissant que les programmes CVE de l'USAID sont informés par des preuves de haute qualité et, en fin de compte, défend la sécurité nationale des États-Unis en facilitant l'apprentissage visant à arrêter la propagation de groupes extrémistes violents qui menacent les intérêts américains. Cette activité contribue directement aux objectifs stratégiques 1.2 (Vaincre l'Etat islamique, Al-Qaida et d'autres organisations terroristes transnationales, et contrer les groupes terroristes parrainés par l'État, régionaux et locaux qui menacent les intérêts de sécurité nationale des États-Unis) et 4.1 (Renforcer l'efficacité et la durabilité de notre diplomatie et de nos investissements dans le développement).

description.narrative: (Cote d'Ivoire): .The Accountability for Development (A4D) activity is designed to address accountability and service delivery challenges in particular related to the lack of civil society influence with government, participatory government-citizen interactions. The purpose of A4D is to engage civil society organizations (CSO) and the government of Côte d'Ivoire (GoCI) at the local and national levels, to reduce underlying sources of conflict and tension in A4D target communities. In May 2020, USAID/Côte d'Ivoire received $1,100,000 of FY 2020 supplemental Economic Support Funds (ESF) to implement a set of activities to increase community resilience to prevent the spread and respond to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in Côte d'Ivoire's rural and urban areas, particularly along trade border and high conflict-risk areas. The DRG team is modifying the A4D activity to include COVID-19 response activities. This will bring the total estimated amount (TEA) of the award to $4,968,397. ..FY 2020 funds will target capacity building, strengthen citizen networks and oversight mechanisms, and address the non-health impact of COVID-19. A4D will work with local champions to identify local service delivery priorities and communicate them to the appropriate officials through innovative approaches. A4D will work with local and regional government entities to respond to increased citizens' demands for tangible outcomes, establish COVID-19 response coordination mechanisms, disseminate accurate information on COVID-19 transmission prevention measures at the community level, and counter disinformation and misinformation through traditional and social media. Finally, USAID will provide targeted economic opportunities and social support to youth and women affected by COVID-19 related travel and trade restrictions along trade and border routes. This activity contributes directly to the ICS Strategic Objective 1.3.... .. .. .. .. ...

title.narrative: Expand Family Planning and Sexual and Reproductive Health (ExpandPF) Activity

description.narrative: The Expand Family Planning and Sexual and Reproductive Health (ExpandPF) Activity will scale up evidence-based family planning practices, including postpartum family planning and engaging community health workers, to improve access to and use of voluntary family planning services in poor and underserved urban and peri-urban populations. ExpandPF envisions a local-partner forward strategy and close engagement with young people for implementation in Cameroon, Cote dIvoire, Mauritania, and Togo. Partners on the project include Options Consultancy Services, Etrilabs, and International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF) member associations in each of the four implementing countries: Association Ivoirienne pour le Bien-tre Familial (AIBEF), Association Togolaise pour le Bien-tre Familial (ATBEF), Association Mauritanienne pour la Promotion de la Famille (AMPF), and Cameroon National Association for Family Welfare (CAMNAFAW). The team also includes Viamo as sub-contractor. Through ExpandPF, the consortium will ultimately assist individuals to make voluntary, informed decisions about family planning with access to contraceptive methods and services.

title.narrative: USAID’s Our Forest, Our Future Activity (USAID’s Msitu Wetu, Umilele Wetu)

description.narrative: (USAID Central Africa Regional): The DRC's Ituri Province is rich in natural resources, including wildlife, forest products, gold, and oil. Many of these resources are illegally extracted, financing armed groups, fueling violence, and threatening conservation efforts. The Okapi Wildlife Reserve (OWR), established in 1992 and listed as a World Heritage Site in 1996, protects the habitat of the okapi and preserves rare plant and animal life, as well as the lifestyle and culture of indigenous people. It is a potential pillar of stability in the region but faces several threats such as illicit mining and poaching that sustain armed groups. To address these challenges, USAID's Our Forest, Our Future Activity (USAID's Msitu Wetu, Umilele Wetu) will promote peacebuilding and stabilization in and around OWR using a People-to-People approach. It will a) illuminate the drivers of conflict and instability around the OWR, b) build community resilience to violence, exploitation, and armed group recruitment c) create incentives for licit economic activity, and d) strengthen peaceful inter-communal ties in and around the OWR. Interventions will support conflict mitigation and reconciliation by creating opportunities for communities in pre-conflict, conflict-affected, and post-conflict situations to build mutual understanding, trust, empathy, and socio-economic resilience to resolve past grievances and mitigate conflict and violence. ..

description.narrative: (South Sudan): Shejeh Salam is USAID's flagship activity working to mitigate sub-national violence and help civil society engage the transitional government in a restricted political space. The project aims to achieve US Government-integrated country strategy goals on subnational violence reduction and peace agreement implementation. The project targets challenges faced by citizens in the 13 target counties promoting dialogue and trauma awareness and expanding access to information through mass media. With FY 2022 funding, Shejeh Salam will award grants, support capacity building, and provide technical assistance to local actors, empowering them to foster stability and peace. Approximately 20 percent of annual funding will go directly to local organizations as grants under contract, contributing towards the USAID Localization approach. Shejeh Salam will also help communities benefiting from community reconciliation by funding activities to promote local economic development resulting from local peace dialogues. Some of the activities will include the construction of shared community assets, and livelihood promotion grants to support women and youth groups participating in peace dialogues. The project will continue to build on lessons learned from over eight years of USAID programming on conflict mitigation and peacebuilding since the outbreak of civil war in 2013. The project will seek out and leverage opinion leaders such as traditional authorities, religious leaders, civil society actors, and media to increase resilience and reduce local communities' manipulation by political elites. Hence, peacebuilding and conflict mitigation cover several volatile intercommunal relationships, predominantly surrounding cattle raiding and revenge killing. The type of conflict dynamic here has political and military support from elite actors in Juba through the provision of arms. ..

title.narrative: Atividade de Apoio à Missão da África Austral (SAMS).

description.narrative: The purpose of the Southern Africa Mission Support (SAMS) activity is to provide program, administrative, financial management and acquisition and assistance support services to USAIDs Missions and offices in the Southern Africa region, including the Power Africa office. The objective of the Southern Africa Mission Support (SAMS) contract is to provide services to USAIDs Missions and offices in the Southern African region, including the Power Africa office, in the areas of program support, administrative, financial management and acquisition and assistance services when needed to ensure USAIDs continuing ability to successfully implement its development assistance activities in the region. This will be accomplished through the following four tasks: Task 1: Program Support Services; Task 2: Administrative Support Services; Task 3: Financial Management Services; Task 4: Acquisition and Assistance Services..

O objectivo da actividade de Apoio à Missão da África Austral (SAMS) é fornecer serviços de apoio programático, administrativo, financeiro e de aquisição e assistência às missões e escritórios da USAID na região da África Austral, incluindo o escritório Power Africa. O objectivo do contrato de Apoio à Missão da África Austral (SAMS) é fornecer serviços às missões e escritórios da USAID na região da África Austral, incluindo o escritório Power Africa, nas áreas de apoio a programas, gestão administrativa, financeira e serviços de aquisição e assistência quando necessário para garantir a capacidade contínua da USAID de implementar com sucesso as suas actividades de assistência ao desenvolvimento na região. Isto será realizado através das seguintes quatro tarefas: Tarefa 1: Serviços de Apoio ao Programa; Tarefa 2: Serviços de Apoio Administrativo; Tarefa 3: Serviços de Gestão Financeira; Tarefa 4: Serviços de Aquisição e Assistência..

title.narrative: Power Africa assistance and engineering consulting services IDIQ

description.narrative: Power Africa contract for transaction advisory services, enabling environment technical support, engineering services and technical assistance that will lead to 30,000 MegaWatts of new generation and 60 million connections in sub-Saharan Africa. Assistance will be rendered under 14 technical areas: 1. Generation, Transmission, and Distribution Transactions; 2. Finance; 3. Legal; 4. Engineering; 5. Planning; 6. Electric Utility Reform and Restructuring; 7. Electricity Access; 8. International Power Exchange and Power Trading; 9. Demand-Side Management and Energy Efficiency; 10. Cleaner Energy Technologies; 11. Gas; 12. Governance; 13. Legal and Regulatory Framework; 14. Coordination and Cooperation.

title.narrative: Power Africa: Nigeria Power Sector Program (NPSP)

description.narrative: (USAID Africa Regional): The Nigeria Power Sector Program (NPSP) seeks comprehensive reform within Nigeria's power sector. USAID AFR Regional FY 2022 funds will support this activity to address gas-to-power challenges; competitive procurement of clean and conventional energy; regulatory and policy reforms; utility distribution sector reform; and off-grid electricity access...To achieve its goals of 10,000 megawatts (MW) and three million new connections to homes and businesses by 2023, NPSP will: 1) continue to provide senior technical advisors to the core Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) beneficiary ministries; 2) provide trainings to the FGN, its agencies, ministries and the private sector; and 3) convene local counterparts to advance policies and build capacity in the electricity supply industry...NPSP will seek to reduce greenhouse emissions by supporting clean energy and flare gas capturing projects. Captured flares will be commercialized for power generation, reducing electricity generation demand from inefficient off-grid, diesel/petrol-fired generators. NPSP will also continue to increase grid capacity, reduce technical losses and enhance operational performance of distribution utilities. This will reduce compensatory generation leading to additional greenhouse gas emissions...NPSP will continue work with the FGN to establish and implement policies that give local and foreign private sector companies, including American companies, a fair chance at competing. Calls for tenders and other opportunities will be disseminated to Power Africa partners and U.S. companies...NPSP will also continue to assist the private sector by building models and providing analysis that increases access to financing...Finally, NPSP will continue to foster enhanced roles for women in power sector institutions by promoting skill development, better hiring practices, increased access to finance for female entrepreneurs, and policy reforms to incorporate gender into energy planning

description.narrative: (USAID Africa Regional): The Power Africa Off-grid Project (PAOP) provides technical assistance and targeted grant funding to support the development of Africa's off-grid solar home system (SHS) and mini-grid sectors. PAOP works with companies, investors, and governments to advance the role of the private sector in extending energy access. The project focuses on 12 countries: Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, and Uganda. Starting in FY 2020, the project has significantly increased the share of support offered to health facility electrification (HFE) in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The program also incentivizes solar energy companies to provide reliable, affordable, off-grid electricity to healthcare facilities in SSA. Energy is critical for powering essential devices, medical and sterilization equipment, diagnostics, cold storage for vaccines and medication, information technology, and lights to enable the delivery of continuous health care services. By offering market intelligence, advising governments on establishing supportive policy frameworks, and providing hands-on support to companies, PAOP helps to build the off-grid market to accelerate private sector-led energy access to health facilities across the continent. PAOP works to ensure that government-sponsored off-grid energy procurements are competitive and transparent, providing an even playing field for all companies, and that quality assurance frameworks are in place to prevent cheap goods from flooding the market. PAOP will continue to provide technical assistance to local renewable energy associations, building their capacity to adopt supply chain practices that promote transparency and economic sovereignty. By supporting off-grid solutions that are powered by solar energy in marginalized communities, PAOP will promote renewable energy, advance energy resilience, energy security, and independence....
Sous-engager des fonds pour l'obligation initiale de la nouvelle activité d'adaptation de l'apprentissage.

(USAID Afrique Régional) : Le projet Power Africa Off-grid (PAOP) fournit une assistance technique et des subventions ciblées pour soutenir le développement des systèmes solaires domestiques hors réseau (SHS) et des secteurs des mini-réseaux en Afrique. Le PAOP travaille avec des entreprises, des investisseurs et des gouvernements pour faire progresser le rôle du secteur privé dans l'extension de l'accès à l'énergie. Le projet se concentre sur 12 pays : Cameroun, Côte d'Ivoire, République démocratique du Congo, Éthiopie, Ghana, Kenya, Libéria, Niger, Rwanda, Sénégal, Tanzanie et Ouganda. À partir de l’exercice 2020, le projet a considérablement augmenté la part du soutien offert à l’électrification des établissements de santé (HFE) en réponse à la pandémie de COVID-19. Le programme encourage également les entreprises d’énergie solaire à fournir une électricité fiable, abordable et hors réseau aux établissements de santé d’ASS. L’énergie est essentielle pour alimenter les appareils essentiels, les équipements médicaux et de stérilisation, les diagnostics, l’entreposage frigorifique des vaccins et des médicaments, les technologies de l’information et l’éclairage pour permettre la prestation continue de services de soins de santé. En offrant des informations sur le marché, en conseillant les gouvernements sur la mise en place de cadres politiques favorables et en fournissant un soutien pratique aux entreprises, le PAOP contribue à construire le marché hors réseau afin d'accélérer l'accès à l'énergie du secteur privé aux établissements de santé à travers le continent. Le PAOP veille à ce que les achats d’énergie hors réseau parrainés par le gouvernement soient compétitifs et transparents, offrant des conditions de concurrence équitables pour toutes les entreprises, et à ce que des cadres d’assurance qualité soient en place pour empêcher les produits bon marché d’inonder le marché. Le PAOP continuera à fournir une assistance technique aux associations locales d’énergies renouvelables, renforçant ainsi leur capacité à adopter des pratiques de chaîne d’approvisionnement qui favorisent la transparence et la souveraineté économique. En soutenant les solutions hors réseau alimentées par l'énergie solaire dans les communautés marginalisées, le PAOP promouvra les énergies renouvelables, fera progresser la résilience énergétique, la sécurité énergétique et l'indépendance....

description.narrative: West Africa blues projects are dedicated to the conservation and restoration of mangrove ecosystems throughout West Africa, with a focus on Guinea and Sierra Leone. The primary goals of these projects are to mitigate the impacts of climate change, protect critical biodiversity, and enhance the livelihoods of local communities. Blues first project in Sierra Leone was recently published as a pipeline listing on verras verified carbon standards (VCS) registry in August 2023 and can be found here. General background information and countries context: according to the USAID - forest carbon, markets and communities (FCMC) project, mangroves in West Africa represent 13% of mangrove forests worldwide and cover more than 2. 4 million hectares across 19 countries. However, the region has experienced a rapid loss of its mangrove cover at a rate of 1. 7% per year. At the same time, coastal communities in West Africa face high poverty levels, inequality, food insecurity, and vulnerability to the impacts of climate change such as sea level rise and coastal erosion. Women in particular face increased economic and social marginalization and climate vulnerability. Blues project areas are home to traditional fishing communities that have turned to mangrove cutting as a way to make income due to depleted fish stocks from foreign trawlers. Mangrove forests in Sierra Leone and Guinea are being deforested due to community members selling mangrove wood or using it for preserving fish through smoking, fuel for cooking, construction purposes, or other uses. Further, mangroves play an essential role as nursery areas for fish and shellfish, which contribute more than $400 million annually to the regional economy. Mangrove forests are also important for stabilizing the shoreline and buffering communities against the impacts of storms and sea level rise. Aider les jeunes et les adultes à acquérir des connaissances et à développer des compétences au-delà de l'alphabétisation et de la numératie de base qui font partie de l'éducation de base, des attitudes et des comportements pour trouver des emplois légitimes, créer des entreprises de travail indépendant viables et rester employés et productifs dans une économie en évolution. description.narrative: The aim of the project is for Nigers civil society to engage the government more effectively, and for key government institutions to be more effective in their mandates and meet the needs of citizens. To do this, SHIGA will strive to achieve three main objectives: Objective 1: Civil society holds responsible government more actively and effectively, and creates demand for targeted reforms and better implementation by the government. FSVC will provide technical assistance to civil society organizations to build their capacity to advocate for reforms. The technical approach is modeled on the incubation paradigm widely used successfully in the private sector for start-ups. Objective 2: Targeted government institutions are more accountable to citizens, and more efficient and transparent in their operations. Capacity building will rely less on formal training and more on learning-by-doing, led by policy experts. Objective 3: Create and/or strengthen spaces for constructive engagement between citizens, civil society and the state to identify and implement targeted priority reforms.

Soutenir la compétition politique pacifique et la négociation des différends par le biais d’un processus politique démocratique et représentatif. Créer et soutenir des véhicules permettant aux gens de débattre des priorités publiques, de proposer des solutions alternatives, d'obtenir le soutien des remèdes proposés et de contribuer aux décisions qui affectent leur vie.

L'objectif du projet est que la société civile nigérienne s'engage plus efficacement avec le gouvernement et que les principales institutions gouvernementales soient plus efficaces dans leurs mandats et répondent aux besoins des citoyens. Pour ce faire, SHIGA s'efforcera d'atteindre trois objectifs principaux : Objectif 1 : La société civile tient un gouvernement responsable de manière plus active et efficace, et crée une demande de réformes ciblées et d'une meilleure mise en œuvre par le gouvernement. Le FSVC fournira une assistance technique aux organisations de la société civile pour renforcer leur capacité à plaider en faveur de réformes. L’approche technique est calquée sur le paradigme de l’incubation largement utilisé avec succès dans le secteur privé pour les start-up. Objectif 2 : Les institutions gouvernementales ciblées sont plus responsables envers les citoyens et plus efficaces et transparentes dans leurs opérations. Le renforcement des capacités reposera moins sur la formation formelle et davantage sur l’apprentissage par la pratique, dirigé par des experts politiques. Objectif 3 : Créer et/ou renforcer des espaces d'engagement constructif entre les citoyens, la société civile et l'État pour identifier et mettre en œuvre des réformes prioritaires ciblées.

SCC will improve CLA among all stakeholders in order to enhance development results and help USAID better communicate those results. description.narrative: To support populations of the Sahel and Central North in strengthening their resilience for the socio-economic development of the areas concerned, and make a strong active and visible plea to local and national authorities to strengthen the issue of land security for agro-sylvo pastoral investments, as well as the inclusion of vulnerable groups.

Le but de l'activité de collaboration et de communication (SCC) au Sahel est de promouvoir la collaboration, l'apprentissage et l'adaptation (CLA) pour un impact collectif entre l'USAID, les partenaires de mise en œuvre des activités RISE II, SDP et Bridge dans les communautés partenaires du Sahel, certaines institutions gouvernementales nationales et les instituts de recherche ; et renforcer les capacités locales d’apprentissage et d’adaptation. Accompagner les populations du Sahel et du Centre Nord dans le renforcement de leur résilience pour le développement socio-économique des zones concernées, et lancer un plaidoyer actif et visible auprès des autorités locales et nationales pour renforcer la question de la sécurisation foncière des investissements agro-sylvopastoraux, ainsi que l'inclusion des groupes vulnérables.

description.narrative: (Niger): USAID is partnering with a private technology firm (NewPath) to implement the USAID Affordable Mobile Phones activity in Niger and Burkina Faso which will significantly enhance USAID's ability to transmit development information to beneficiaries. This activity will promote low-cost leasing, use, and ownership of smartphones in USAID zones of influence. The smartphones will be pre-loaded with content focused on agricultural services, health messaging, literacy and numeracy, citizen rights and duties, and other key USAID-supported technical areas. The activity will enable beneficiaries to lease smartphones for the equivalent of a few dollars a month, with the end users later owning the devices when a sufficient number of payments have been made. .USAID decided to partner with NewPath because the company's technology provides the ability to reduce functionality if leasing payments are missed, thereby incentivizing on-time lease payment. Through this activity USAID will gain the ability to target communications to specific beneficiaries in specific geographies to bolster existing programming and contribute to Mission Objective 3.1: Investment and broad-based employment are increased, leading to growth and diversification of Niger's economy. Additionally, USAID's agriculture activities will be able to more cheaply and efficiently transmit information to farmers on pest management or climate information in specific parts of the country if need be and USAID's countering violent extremism activities in the region will also be able to communicate much more effectively with specific target audiences. .This activity supports the Journey to Self-Reliance by engaging the private sector in addressing development needs and by empowering individuals through knowledge sharing. .

Accompagner les populations du Sahel et du Centre Nord dans le renforcement de leur résilience pour le développement socio-économique des zones concernées, et lancer un plaidoyer actif et visible auprès des autorités locales et nationales pour renforcer la question de la sécurisation foncière des investissements agro-sylvopastoraux, ainsi que l'inclusion des groupes vulnérables.

(Niger) : L'USAID s'associe à une entreprise technologique privée (NewPath) pour mettre en œuvre l'activité de téléphonie mobile abordable de l'USAID au Niger et au Burkina Faso, ce qui améliorera considérablement la capacité de l'USAID à transmettre des informations sur le développement aux bénéficiaires. Cette activité encouragera la location, l'utilisation et la possession à faible coût de smartphones dans les zones d'influence de l'USAID. Les smartphones seront préchargés avec du contenu axé sur les services agricoles, les messages de santé, l'alphabétisation et le calcul, les droits et devoirs des citoyens, ainsi que d'autres domaines techniques clés soutenus par l'USAID. L'activité permettra aux bénéficiaires de louer des smartphones pour l'équivalent de quelques dollars par mois, les utilisateurs finaux devenant ensuite propriétaires des appareils lorsqu'un nombre suffisant de paiements aura été effectué. .USAID a décidé de s'associer à NewPath car la technologie de l'entreprise offre la possibilité de réduire les fonctionnalités en cas de manquement aux paiements de loyer, encourageant ainsi le paiement du loyer à temps. Grâce à cette activité, l'USAID aura la capacité de cibler les communications vers des bénéficiaires spécifiques dans des zones géographiques spécifiques afin de renforcer les programmes existants et de contribuer à l'objectif de mission 3.1 : Les investissements et l'emploi généralisé sont accrus, conduisant à la croissance et à la diversification de l'économie du Niger. De plus, les activités agricoles de l'USAID seront en mesure de transmettre, à moindre coût et plus efficacement, des informations aux agriculteurs sur la lutte antiparasitaire ou des informations climatiques dans des régions spécifiques du pays si nécessaire et les activités de lutte contre l'extrémisme violent de l'USAID dans la région seront également en mesure de communiquer beaucoup plus efficacement avec des publics cibles spécifiques. .Cette activité soutient le parcours vers l’autonomie en engageant le secteur privé à répondre aux besoins de développement et en responsabilisant les individus grâce au partage des connaissances. .

description.narrative: Water Security and Resilience (WSR) Activity will be implemented in Niger and Burkina Faso as part of the Resilience in the Sahel Enhanced (RISE) II program and the Sahel Development Partnership (SDP). WSR is an integral component of USAIDs RISE II program in Burkina Faso and Niger, designed to address the root causes of chronic vulnerabilitywhich is defined as an enduring susceptibility to the effects of constant and cyclical external shocks on life and livelihoods, resulting in persistent food and water insecurity.

Activité de soutien électoral au Niger pour promouvoir une transition démocratique pacifique à travers des élections libres, transparentes et inclusives dans le cadre du LWA pour les élections mondiales et les transitions politiques (GEPT).

L'activité de sécurité de l'eau et de résilience (WSR) sera mise en œuvre au Niger et au Burkina Faso dans le cadre du programme Résilience renforcée au Sahel (RISE) II et du Partenariat de développement du Sahel (SDP). WSR fait partie intégrante du programme RISE II de l'USAID au Burkina Faso et au Niger, conçu pour s'attaquer aux causes profondes de la vulnérabilité chronique, définie comme une susceptibilité persistante aux effets de chocs externes constants et cycliques sur la vie et les moyens de subsistance, entraînant une insécurité alimentaire et hydrique persistante.

title.narrative: USAID Kulawa Activity for implementation of Health Services Delivery Activity in the Republic of Niger
Activité de l'USAID Kulawa pour la mise en œuvre de l'activité de prestation de services de santé en République du Niger.
Activité de l'USAID Kulawa pour la mise en œuvre de l'activité de prestation de services de santé en République du Niger.
Activité de l'USAID Kulawa pour la mise en œuvre de l'activité de prestation de services de santé en République du Niger.

description.narrative: The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Kulawa activity is a five-year (2020-2025) award to support the Government of Niger in improving health, family planning, and nutrition outcomes in the Maradi, Zinder, and Tillaberi regions. Meaning care in the Hausa language, Kulawa will collaborate with the Ministry of Health, local government, providers, and communities to implement activities that will reach 1.4 million women of reproductive age, 1.1 million children under five years old, and 2.6 million youth ages 15-35. Kulawa is part of USAIDs Resilience in the Sahel Enhanced (RISE) project, which supports vulnerable communities in Niger to effectively prepare for and manage recurrent crises and pursue sustainable pathways out of poverty.
Réquisition pour l'attribution de l'activité d'atténuation et de réconciliation des conflits "On est ensemble" au Niger.

L'activité Kulawa de l'Agence des États-Unis pour le développement international (USAID) est une récompense quinquennale (2020-2025) visant à soutenir le gouvernement du Niger dans l'amélioration des résultats en matière de santé, de planification familiale et de nutrition dans les régions de Maradi, Zinder et Tillabéri. Kulawa, qui signifie soins en langue haoussa, collaborera avec le ministère de la Santé, le gouvernement local, les prestataires et les communautés pour mettre en œuvre des activités qui toucheront 1,4 million de femmes en âge de procréer, 1,1 million d'enfants de moins de cinq ans et 2,6 millions de jeunes âgés de 15 à 35 ans. Kulawa fait partie du projet Resilience in the Sahel Enhanced (RISE) de l'USAID, qui aide les communautés vulnérables du Niger à se préparer et à gérer efficacement les crises récurrentes et à poursuivre des voies durables pour sortir de la pauvreté.

L'activité Kulawa de l'Agence des États-Unis pour le développement international (USAID) est une récompense quinquennale (2020-2025) visant à soutenir le gouvernement du Niger dans l'amélioration des résultats en matière de santé, de planification familiale et de nutrition dans les régions de Maradi, Zinder et Tillabéri. title.narrative: Activité de prestation de services de santé
Activité de prestation de services de santé

description.narrative: Health Services Delivery award for Burkina Faso

L'activité Kulawa de l'Agence des États-Unis pour le développement international (USAID) est une récompense quinquennale (2020-2025) visant à soutenir le gouvernement du Niger dans l'amélioration des résultats en matière de santé, de planification familiale et de nutrition dans les régions de Maradi, Zinder et Tillabéri. Kulawa, qui signifie soins en langue haoussa, collaborera avec le ministère de la Santé, le gouvernement local, les prestataires et les communautés pour mettre en œuvre des activités qui toucheront 1,4 million de femmes en âge de procréer, 1,1 million d'enfants de moins de cinq ans et 2,6 millions de jeunes âgés de 15 à 35 ans. Kulawa fait partie du projet Resilience in the Sahel Enhanced (RISE) de l'USAID, qui aide les communautés vulnérables du Niger à se préparer et à gérer efficacement les crises récurrentes et à poursuivre des voies durables pour sortir de la pauvreté.
Prix ​​de la prestation des services de santé pour le Burkina Faso.

title.narrative: Burkina Faso Human Rights and Access to Justice Activity (USAID BFHR)
Activité relative aux droits de l'homme et à l'accès à la justice au Burkina Faso (USAID BFHR)
Activité relative aux droits de l'homme et à l'accès à la justice au Burkina Faso (USAID BFHR)

description.narrative: (Burkina Faso): ..The USAID Burkina Faso Human Rights and Access to Justice (HRAJ) activity is addressing development challenges related to vulnerability to violent extremism. HRAJ will support sub-Intermediate Results related to human rights and access to justice under Bridge Objective 2: Government Legitimacy Enhanced. With FY 20201 funding, USAID will work with the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) to address human rights violations and support civil society to play the role of watchdog through advocacy, reporting, and documentation. .Through this activity, USAID will help the CNDH to improve its capacity, provide training on legal procedures to address human rights violations, provide IT equipment to improve management of information about alleged human rights violations, and stand up a Public Outreach Center to increase transparency. USAID will strengthen civil society's capacity and provide small grants to document alleged human rights violations and conduct advocacy and public outreach. This activity will also help the bar association improve legal aid services, including through training on victim and witness protection, use and handling of evidence, and overall case intake and management processes. USAID, through Freedom House, will also develop Atrocity Prevention Protocols to be shared with CNDH and civil society organisations. Freedom House was selected because they are an international leader in human rights, and have provided this type of assistance successfully in many other countries..USAID HRAJ directly addresses Mission Objective 1.2 "Reduce the influence of violent extremism in the Sahel" by addressing drivers of support for extremist groups, i.e. pervasive human rights violations. $500,000 of funding under this IM contributes to meeting the required democracy programs earmark of $2,000,000, and $300,000 of funding contributes to meeting the required countering violent extremism earmark..

L'objectif de ce programme est d'aider un bénéficiaire à mettre en œuvre un programme visant à faire des progrès significatifs dans l'objectif global d'atténuation des conflits, de paix et de réconciliation grâce à la mise en œuvre du P2P.

(Burkina Faso) : ..L'activité droits de l'homme et accès à la justice (HRAJ) de l'USAID Burkina Faso aborde les défis de développement liés à la vulnérabilité à l'extrémisme violent. HRAJ soutiendra les résultats sous-intermédiaires liés aux droits de l’homme et à l’accès à la justice dans le cadre de l’Objectif Bridge 2 : Légitimité du gouvernement renforcée. Grâce au financement de l'exercice 20201, l'USAID travaillera avec la Commission nationale des droits de l'homme (CNDH) pour lutter contre les violations des droits de l'homme et aider la société civile à jouer le rôle de chien de garde à travers le plaidoyer, le reporting et la documentation. Grâce à cette activité, l'USAID aidera le CNDH à améliorer ses capacités, à dispenser une formation sur les procédures juridiques visant à traiter les violations des droits de l'homme, à fournir des équipements informatiques pour améliorer la gestion des informations sur les violations présumées des droits de l'homme et à créer un centre de sensibilisation du public pour accroître la transparence. L'USAID renforcera les capacités de la société civile et fournira de petites subventions pour documenter les violations présumées des droits de l'homme et mener des activités de plaidoyer et de sensibilisation du public. Cette activité aidera également le barreau à améliorer les services d'aide juridique, notamment par le biais de formations sur la protection des victimes et des témoins, l'utilisation et le traitement des preuves, ainsi que sur les processus globaux d'admission et de gestion des dossiers. L'USAID, par l'intermédiaire de Freedom House, élaborera également des protocoles de prévention des atrocités qui seront partagés avec le CNDH et les organisations de la société civile. Freedom House a été sélectionnée parce qu'elle est un leader international en matière de droits de l'homme et a fourni ce type d'assistance avec succès dans de nombreux autres pays. L'USAID HRAJ répond directement à l'objectif de mission 1.2 « Réduire l'influence de l'extrémisme violent au Sahel » en s'attaquant aux facteurs de soutien aux groupes extrémistes, c'est-à-dire aux violations généralisées des droits de l'homme. Un financement de 500 000 $ dans le cadre de cette GI contribue à atteindre l'affectation requise de 2 000 000 $ pour les programmes de démocratie, et un financement de 300 000 $ contribue à atteindre l'affectation requise pour la lutte contre l'extrémisme violent..

title.narrative: Niger Access to Justice and Human Rights (Adalci)
Niger Accès à la Justice et aux Droits de l'Homme (Adalci)
Niger Accès à la Justice et aux Droits de l'Homme (Adalci)

description.narrative: (Niger): .The Niger Access to Justice and Human Rights Activity or "Adalci" in Hausa language, is designed to provide communities tools to address core grievances driving vulnerability to extremism in the conflict-affected regions of Diffa, Tahoua, and Tillaberi. The activity aims to improve the capacity of customary and other local conflict mediation mechanisms to address grievances and resolve disputes; empower populations in violent extremism (VE) prone areas to navigate and access the formal justice system to resolve disputes or assert their rights; and increase the capacity of government and civil society organizations to address VE-related human rights violations committed by both state and non-state actors...With FY 2022 funds, Adalci will strengthen traditional chiefs and local conflict mediation mechanisms through capacity building, networking, learning, and collaboration. Adalci will support 60 master trainers and community mediators to train 60 additional master trainers, who will in turn train 200 traditional leaders and local mediators in five new target communes. They will work to solve and manage conflicts through intra- and inter- community dialogues and public forums. Adalci will support justice hubs to provide legal aid and referrals to appointed public defenders. They will also work to improve case management, criminal hearings to address extended pre-trial detention, and mobile legal aid clinics. Adalci will support the National Human Rights Commission and CSOs to address human rights issues and collaboration between CSOs, justice actors, and relevant authorities...This activity contributes to Niger MO 1.2: Access to justice and respect for fundamental human rights improves; and MO 2.2: Niger's government institutions, security forces, and civil society collaborate to reduce vulnerability to violent extremism..

(Burkina Faso) : ..L'activité droits de l'homme et accès à la justice (HRAJ) de l'USAID Burkina Faso aborde les défis de développement liés à la vulnérabilité à l'extrémisme violent. Un financement de 500 000 $ dans le cadre de cette GI contribue à atteindre l'affectation requise de 2 000 000 $ pour les programmes de démocratie, et un financement de 300 000 $ contribue à atteindre l'affectation requise pour la lutte contre l'extrémisme violent..

(Niger) : L'activité d'accès à la justice et aux droits de l'homme au Niger ou « Adalci » en langue haoussa, est conçue pour fournir aux communautés des outils pour répondre aux principaux griefs qui conduisent à la vulnérabilité à l'extrémisme dans les régions touchées par le conflit de Diffa, Tahoua et Tillaberi. L'activité vise à améliorer la capacité des mécanismes de médiation coutumiers et autres mécanismes locaux de médiation des conflits à traiter les griefs et à résoudre les différends ; donner aux populations des zones sujettes à l’extrémisme violent (EV) les moyens de naviguer et d’accéder au système judiciaire formel pour résoudre les différends ou faire valoir leurs droits ; et accroître la capacité du gouvernement et des organisations de la société civile à lutter contre les violations des droits humains liées à l'extrémisme violent commises par des acteurs étatiques et non étatiques... Avec les fonds de l'exercice 2022, Adalci renforcera les chefs traditionnels et les mécanismes locaux de médiation des conflits grâce au renforcement des capacités, au réseautage, à l'apprentissage et à la collaboration. Adalci appuiera 60 maîtres formateurs et médiateurs communautaires pour former 60 maîtres formateurs supplémentaires, qui formeront à leur tour 200 chefs traditionnels et médiateurs locaux dans cinq nouvelles communes cibles. Ils s’efforceront de résoudre et de gérer les conflits à travers des dialogues intra- et intercommunautaires et des forums publics. Adalci soutiendra les centres de justice pour fournir une aide juridique et des orientations vers des défenseurs publics désignés. Ils s’efforceront également d’améliorer la gestion des dossiers, les audiences pénales pour traiter la détention provisoire prolongée et les cliniques mobiles d’aide juridique. Adalci soutiendra la Commission nationale des droits de l'homme et les OSC pour aborder les questions de droits de l'homme et la collaboration entre les OSC, les acteurs de la justice et les autorités compétentes... Cette activité contribue à l'OM 1.2 du Niger : L'accès à la justice et le respect des droits humains fondamentaux s'améliorent ; et MO 2.2 : Les institutions gouvernementales, les forces de sécurité et la société civile du Niger collaborent pour réduire la vulnérabilité à l'extrémisme violent..

description.narrative: The Youth Connect activity seeks to equip vulnerable young women and men in Niger with the skills, networks, and capital for increased strategic economic opportunities.
